definition_zh: 错过；未击中；想念；察觉缺失；（Miss）小姐
definition_en: to fail to hit, catch, reach or attend something, to feel sad because someone is absent, and, as a separate title, to address an unmarried woman
core_image: 一支箭擦着靶边飞过，靶心还空着
scene: 站台上人群已经跑得气喘，铁门却在眼前合拢。We sprinted for the platform, but the doors closed and we missed the evening train.
sceneCN: 这里是「错过车次」（第 2 个义项：太晚而失去班次）；句意为两人冲向站台，门已关上，错过了晚间那班车。图中可辨识物件：站台铁门、奔跑的人群、末班车的灯光。

pos.zh: 错过；未击中；想念；察觉缺失

derivatives.zh: 由 miss 加 -ing 构成，指不在原处、缺失或失踪的
由过去分词转作形容词，指被错过、未能抓住的
由 miss 加 -able 构成，指可以略过、不值得一看的

senses.title: To fail to hit or catch a target
senses.definition: to aim at something and fail to touch it, catch it or land on it
senses.definitionCN: 瞄准某物却没能碰到、接住或落在上面
senses.example: He swung at the ball but missed it completely.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝球挥棒，却完全没打中。
senses.why: Old English missan described a shot or a blow that went wide of its mark, and that physical failure to connect is the picture every later sense keeps borrowing.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 missan 最早说的是一箭或一击偏了靶心、没能碰上目标；这种身体上「没接上」的画面，是后面每个义项一直在借用的起点。

senses.title: To be too late for a train, bus or chance
senses.definition: to arrive too late for a bus, train or opportunity, so that it is lost
senses.definitionCN: 到达得太晚，没能赶上公交、火车或机会，于是失去它
senses.example: We ran for the platform but missed the last train.
senses.exampleCN: 我们朝站台跑过去，却错过了最后一班火车。
senses.why: A train leaves on its own timetable, so missing it repeats the same failure to connect, now measured in minutes rather than in inches.
senses.whyCN: 列车按自己的时刻表开走，「错过」还是那次没接上，只是衡量的尺度从几寸变成了几分钟，于是同一个词从靶场挪到了站台。

senses.title: To feel sad because someone is absent
senses.definition: to feel unhappy because a person or thing you care about is not with you
senses.definitionCN: 因为牵挂的人或物不在身边而感到难过
senses.example: She missed her family more than she had expected.
senses.exampleCN: 她想念家人的程度超出了自己的预料。
senses.why: Since missan could also mean to be without something, the verb could name the ache of that absence; the target you fail to reach becomes a person you fail to keep near.
senses.whyCN: 既然 missan 还能表示「身边没有某物」，这个词就可以指那份缺席带来的空落；没能击中的目标，变成了没能守在身边的人。

senses.title: To notice that something is not there
senses.definition: to notice that a thing or person is no longer in its usual place
senses.definitionCN: 察觉到某物或某人已不在原来的位置
senses.example: I missed my wallet only when I reached the till.
senses.exampleCN: 直到走到收银台，我才发现钱包不见了。
senses.why: A hand still reaches for the pocket where the wallet always sits, and the empty place is what the eye reports; the sense turns absence into a small act of noticing.
senses.whyCN: 手仍按老习惯伸向总放钱包的口袋，眼睛报告的是那块空处；这一层把「缺少」变成了一个察觉的动作。

senses.title: A title for an unmarried woman
senses.definition: a title placed before the surname of an unmarried woman, or used in direct address
senses.definitionCN: 放在未婚女子姓氏之前、或用于当面称呼的称谓
senses.example: Miss Adams teaches the youngest class.
senses.exampleCN: 亚当斯小姐教年纪最小的那个班。
senses.why: This title is a different word altogether, a shortened form of mistress, which once meant a woman in charge; as mistress narrowed, the clipped form kept only the neutral address, which is why it merely looks like the verb.
senses.whyCN: 这个称谓其实是另一个词：mistress 的缩略，本指「掌家的女人」；后来 mistress 词义收窄，缩略形式只留下中性的称呼，所以它只是碰巧和动词长得一样。

intro.en: Miss is a Germanic verb for going wide of a mark; it reached English before the Norman conquest, and a separate word later shrank into the title Miss.
intro.cn: miss 是日耳曼语中表示「偏出目标」的动词，在诺曼征服之前就进入英语；另有一个与它无关的词后来缩略成了称谓 Miss。

items.en: The reconstructed form *missijan- meant to go wrong or to fail to reach, and it is the common ancestor of the Germanic verbs of missing.
items.cn: *missijan- 是重构形式，意为「走岔、没能到达」，是日耳曼语各语支里「错过」类动词的共同祖先。

items.en: Old English missan meant to fail to hit or reach something, and it could also mean to be without it.
items.cn: 古英语 missan 意为没能击中或到达某物，也可以指身边没有它。

items.en: Middle English kept both strands alive: failing to hit a target and lacking something that ought to be there.
items.cn: 中古英语把两条线都留着：既指没打中目标，也指缺了本该有的东西。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the verb was used for feeling a person's absence, while the noun a miss named a shot that went wide.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个动词已经用来表示感到某人不在身边；名词 a miss 则指打偏的一击。

items.en: Modern English keeps the verb for targets, timetables and absent people; the title Miss is a shortening of mistress, a different word that merely looks the same.
items.cn: 现代英语让这个动词负责目标、时刻表与缺席的人；称谓 Miss 是 mistress 的缩略，来历不同，只是碰巧长得一样。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived form and the shared mis- prefix, including a word that only borrows the prefix; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of losing, skipping and failing to notice.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与共用的 mis- 前缀，也包括只借了前缀的词；近义组收表示失去、跳过与没留意的动词。

entries.definition: The present participle of miss used as an adjective: not in the expected place.
entries.definitionCN: miss 的现在分词转作形容词，指不在原处；缺失的。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning wrongly or badly, the same sideways idea that lives inside miss.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「错误地、不当」的前缀，和 miss 里那股「偏了」的意味一脉相承。

entries.definition: A wrong act or judgement; it uses mis- but its stem comes from Norse taka, so it is no relative of miss.
entries.definitionCN: 错误的行为或判断；它用了 mis- 前缀，但词干来自北欧语的 taka，与 miss 并非同族。

entries.definition: To spell a word wrongly; built from mis- and spell, with no link to the verb beyond the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 把单词拼错；由 mis- 加 spell 构成，除前缀外与动词 miss 没有关系。

entries.definition: To no longer have something, often because it slips away.
entries.definitionCN: 不再拥有某物，常因它溜走而失去。

entries.definition: To leave something out or stay away from it on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 有意略过某事或不去参加。

entries.definition: To fail to notice something that is there in plain view.
entries.definitionCN: 没能注意到就摆在眼前的东西。

entries.definition: To want someone or something very much, especially someone who is absent.
entries.definitionCN: 非常渴望某人或某物，尤指不在身边的人。

normalIntro.en: The verb began as an arrow going wide of its mark, and the whole family keeps that sideways step in view.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词从一支偏出靶心的箭开始，整个词族始终盯着那一步「偏到一边」。

normal.en: Old English missan already meant to go wide of a mark, so every sense begins with a shot that does not land.
normal.cn: 古英语 missan 本就说「偏了靶心」，所以每个义项都从一支没落地的箭开始。

normal.en: The prefix mis- carries the same sideways idea, which is why mistake and misspell both describe a step to the wrong side.
normal.cn: 前缀 mis- 带着同样的「偏到一边」的意味，所以 mistake 与 misspell 都描述走错一步。

normal.en: Miss the bus keeps the archery picture alive: the bus was the mark, and you arrived after it moved.
normal.cn: miss the bus 把射箭的画面留着：车就是靶，你到的时候它已经走了。

normal.en: Missing adds -ing and turns the failure into a state: what is missing is simply not where it belongs.
normal.cn: missing 加 -ing，把「没打中」变成一种状态：missing 的东西就是不在它该在的地方。

normal.en: The title Miss is a clipped mistress, a completely separate word, so it carries no sense of failing to hit anything.
normal.cn: 称谓 Miss 是 mistress 的缩略，完全是另一个词，所以它跟「没打中」毫无关系。

abstract.en: A word that starts with an arrow in the air ends up naming the ache of an empty room, which shows how far one failure can travel.
abstract.cn: 一个从空中飞箭开始的词，最后指称空房间里的那种酸楚，说明一次「没碰上」能走多远。

abstract.en: Missing a train and missing a person both leave a gap where something should have been.
abstract.cn: 错过一班车和想念一个人，都在本该有东西的位置留下空白。

abstract.en: The title sitting beside the verb is a reminder that identical shapes can hide unrelated histories.
abstract.cn: 同一个拼写旁边站着动词和称谓，提醒人：相同的形状可以藏着毫不相干的来历。

examples.en: He reached for the ball and missed it by a finger.
examples.cn: 他伸手去接球，只差一指没接住。

examples.en: I missed the early bus and walked to school.
examples.cn: 我错过了早班车，只好走去学校。

examples.en: She missed her brother most on quiet evenings.
examples.cn: 安静的傍晚，她最想念哥哥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「觅思」——想「觅」却只能「思」，正是错过与想念的滋味。

root: 古英语 missan（没击中、没到达），属日耳曼语族，更早为重构形式 *missijan-（走岔）；与拉丁语 mittere 并非同源，只是形近。称谓 Miss 另出 mistress 的缩略。

sensesIntro.en: The physical failure to hit comes first; the senses then move to a timetable, to a person who is absent, to a gap noticed in a pocket, and finally to a title that merely shares the spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是身体上没击中；义项接着走向时刻表、走向不在身边的人、走向口袋里的空处，最后走向一个只是碰巧同形的称谓。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow passing the edge of the target while the centre stays empty.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭擦着靶边飞过，靶心还空着。

branches.en: a bat swinging past a ball and finding only air
branches.cn: 球棒挥过球旁，只扫到空气

branches.en: a platform gate closing just before a late runner
branches.cn: 站台门在迟到者面前合拢

branches.en: an empty chair kept for someone far away
branches.cn: 为远方的人留着的一把空椅

branches.en: a hand patting a pocket where the wallet should be
branches.cn: 手拍向本该放钱包的口袋

branches.en: a classroom door with a surname written on it
branches.cn: 教室门上写着一个姓氏

intro.en: The word rests on an Old English verb of going wide, the prefix mis-, and a set of English endings that build new forms and relatives.
intro.cn: 这个词靠一个表示「偏出」的古英语动词、前缀 mis-，以及一组造出新形式与同族词的英语词尾支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for miss; the word belongs to the Germanic branch, and the similar-looking Latin mittere is a false friend.
latinIntro.cn: miss 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它属于日耳曼语这一支，形似的拉丁语 mittere 只是一个假朋友。

items.meaning: to fail to hit, to go wrong

definition_zh: 使命；任务；（派往国外的）代表团；传教工作；飞行或军事任务
definition_en: a task that a person or group is sent to carry out, or the purpose an organization sets for itself
core_image: 一个人把封好的信交到另一个人手里，那人转身就上路
scene: 山里的诊所缺药，一支小队带着箱子走了两天，把药送到村口就返回。The team's mission was to reach the village before the rains.
sceneCN: 这里 mission 指被派出去要完成的一项具体任务（第 1 个义项：受派执行的任务）；句意：这支小队的任务是赶在雨季前抵达那个村子。图中可辨识物件：药箱、山路、封好的指令、雨云；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 使命；任务；代表团；传教；飞行任务

derivatives.zh: 传教士；传教的
使命宣言
任务控制中心
委员会；委托
解散；解雇

senses.title: An organization's declared purpose
senses.titleCN: 一个组织公开宣告的宗旨
senses.definition: the purpose that an organization states as its reason for existing
senses.definitionCN: 一个组织声明为其存在理由的宗旨
senses.example: The mission on the clinic wall is one sentence long.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所墙上的宗旨只有一句话。
senses.why: A body that is sent must know what it was sent for, so the word came to mean a declared purpose.
senses.whyCN: 被派出去的团体必须知道自己为何被派，这个词于是也指公开宣告的宗旨。

senses.title: A journey with a set purpose
senses.titleCN: 带有明确目的的一次出行
senses.definition: a journey or trip undertaken to carry out a particular task
senses.definitionCN: 为完成某项特定任务而进行的行程
senses.example: The supply mission took two days over the pass.
senses.exampleCN: 那次补给任务翻过山口用了两天。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a sending: someone is dispatched, and the going is the task.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「被派出」：有人被派遣出去，走这一趟就是任务。

senses.title: A group sent abroad
senses.definition: a group of officials sent to another country to represent their government
senses.definitionCN: 被派往他国代表本国政府的官员团体
senses.example: The trade mission met three buyers in one week.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易代表团一周内见了三位买家。
senses.why: When the sending is diplomatic, the word names the people who were sent rather than the errand.
senses.whyCN: 当派遣是外交性质时，这个词指被派出去的人，而不是那件差事。

senses.title: Religious work or a station
senses.definition: the work of spreading a faith, or the settlement where that work is based
senses.definitionCN: 传播信仰的工作，或这项工作所在的驻地
senses.example: The mission ran a school and a small hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 那个传教站办了一所学校和一间小医院。
senses.why: Missionaries were sent, so their posting took the name of the sending.
senses.whyCN: 传教士是被派出去的，因此他们的驻地沿用了「派遣」这个名字。

senses.title: A military operation with an objective
senses.titleCN: 有明确目标的军事行动
senses.definition: a single operation with a stated objective, often by aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 一次有既定目标的行动，常指飞机出动
senses.example: The squadron flew nine missions in a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个中队一个月里飞了九次任务。
senses.why: An aircrew is sent out with an objective, and the flight becomes the mission.
senses.whyCN: 机组带着目标被派出，这次飞行就成了 mission。

senses.title: A personal calling
senses.definition: the duty that a person feels bound to fulfil in life
senses.definitionCN: 一个人觉得自己一生必须完成的职责
senses.example: Her mission was to teach girls in villages to read.
senses.exampleCN: 她的使命是教村里的女孩识字。
senses.why: A sending can come from inside rather than from a sender, and the word then means a calling.
senses.whyCN: 派遣也可以来自内心而不是来自派遣者，这个词于是指一种召唤。

senses.title: An embassy or delegation office
senses.titleCN: 使馆或代表处的办公机构
senses.definition: the office or building of a country's representative abroad
senses.definitionCN: 一国驻外代表所在的办公机构或馆舍
senses.example: The visa section is on the second floor of the mission.
senses.exampleCN: 签证处在代表处的二楼。
senses.why: The people sent need a place to work, and the building takes the name of the group.
senses.whyCN: 被派出去的人需要一个办公的地方，馆舍便沿用了这群人的名称。

senses.title: A task given to one person
senses.titleCN: 交给某一个人的具体差事
senses.definition: a particular errand or job assigned to an individual
senses.definitionCN: 分配给某一个人的具体差事
senses.example: His mission for the afternoon was to find the missing file.
senses.exampleCN: 他下午的差事是把那份不见的档案找出来。
senses.why: The word scales down to one person and one errand, keeping the same shape of being sent.
senses.whyCN: 这个词能缩小到一个人、一件差事，仍然保持「被派出」的形状。

intro.en: Mission comes from Latin missio 'a sending', built on mittere 'to send'. English first used it for the sending of envoys and missionaries, and later for any task someone is sent to do.
intro.cn: mission 来自拉丁 missio「派遣」，由 mittere「发送」构成。英语最初用它指派遣使节与传教士，后来才指任何被派去完成的任务。

items.en: Latin mittere 'to send, let go' is well recorded, but its deeper origin is uncertain and no older root can be stated with confidence.
items.cn: 拉丁 mittere「发送、放出」记录充分，但其更早来源不确定，无法有把握地给出更古老的词根。

items.en: The past participle missus 'sent' supplies the miss- inside mission, missionary and missile.
items.cn: 过去分词 missus「被送出的」提供了 mission、missionary 与 missile 里的 miss-。

items.en: Missio meant a sending or a letting go; in military Latin it could also mean a discharge from service.
items.cn: missio 意为派遣或放行；在军事拉丁语里也可指解除兵役。

items.en: English took mission in the sixteenth century, first for the sending of envoys, then for the sending of missionaries.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 mission，先指派遣使节，再指派遣传教士。

items.en: By the seventeenth century a mission could be the station itself, and by the eighteenth a permanent embassy.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，mission 可指传教站本身；到十八世纪，又可指常设使馆。

items.en: Aviation, space flight and management gave the word its operation and purpose senses in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 航空、航天与管理在二十世纪赋予这个词「行动」与「宗旨」两义。

note.en: The first group shares the miss- root; the second group names other tasks and purposes.
note.cn: 第一组共享 miss- 词根；第二组是其他任务与宗旨的说法。

entries.definition: From missus 'sent', but it names a weapon that is thrown or fired, not a task.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 missus「被送出的」，但指被投出或发射的武器，不是任务。

entries.definition: From dis- 'away' plus mittere 'send', meaning to send away or let go.
entries.definitionCN: 由 dis-「离开」加 mittere「发送」构成，意为打发走、解散。

entries.definition: From trans- 'across' plus mittere, meaning to send across.
entries.definitionCN: 由 trans-「越过」加 mittere 构成，意为发送过去。

entries.definition: From com- 'together' plus mittere, meaning to entrust a task or the body entrusted with it.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 mittere 构成，意为委托任务，或指受托的机构。

entries.definition: A piece of work to be done, with no idea of being sent.
entries.definitionCN: 一件要做的工作，不含「被派出」之意。

entries.definition: Work given to a person by someone in authority; it stresses the giving.
entries.definitionCN: 由有权者交给某人的工作，强调交付。

entries.definition: The aim behind an action, which is the first sense of mission within an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 行动背后的目标，正是 mission 在组织内部的第一义。

entries.definition: A group sent with authority to represent others, close to the diplomatic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 受权代表他人而被派出的团体，接近外交义。

entries.definition: A strong sense of being called to a kind of work, close to the personal sense.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈感到被召唤去做某类工作，接近个人天职义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Mittere is to send, and missio is a sending, so a mission is literally something sent.
normal.cn: mittere 是发送，missio 是派遣，因此 mission 字面上就是「被派出的事」。

normal.en: The family runs mission, missionary, missile, dismiss and transmit.
normal.cn: 同族词有 missionary、missile、dismiss 与 transmit。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: mission statement, rescue mission, space mission.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出它的用法：使命宣言、救援任务、太空飞行任务。

normal.en: The same word scales from a whole organisation's purpose down to one afternoon errand.
normal.cn: 同一个词能从整个组织的宗旨缩小到一个下午的差事。

normal.en: A sending needs a sender, a message and a road, which is the whole picture.
normal.cn: 一次派遣需要派遣者、消息与一条路，这就是整幅画面。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed letter handed over and a traveller turning at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一封封好的信被交出，旅人当场转身。

abstract.en: Picture a box carried two days over a pass, never set down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只箱子翻过山口走了两天，始终没有放下。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp left burning at a station for those still on the road.
abstract.cn: 想象传教站里为还在路上的人留着一盏灯。

examples.en: The agency rewrote its mission after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水之后，这个机构重写了它的宗旨。

examples.en: A medical mission reached the island on the third day.
examples.cn: 一支医疗队第三天抵达了这座岛。

examples.en: Her mission for the morning was to find the missing key.
examples.cn: 她上午的差事是找到那把不见了的钥匙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「miss（送出）+ ion（名词）」——被送出去要做的事，就是任务

root: 拉丁 mittere「发送」→ 过去分词 missus「被送出的」→ missio「派遣」→ 英语 mission。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with a sending: an organization's declared purpose, a purposeful journey, a group sent abroad, a mission station, a military sortie, a personal calling, an embassy office and one person's errand.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一次派遣开始：组织宣告的宗旨、有目的的出行、派往国外的团体、传教站、军事出动、个人天职、使馆馆舍，以及一个人的差事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed letter handed over, and a traveller who turns and leaves at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一封封好的信被交出，旅人转身立刻出发。

branches.en: WHY AND BY WHOM: a declared purpose, and a calling that feels like a sender inside.
branches.cn: 为何与由谁：公开宣告的宗旨，以及像内心派遣者一样的召唤。

branches.en: THE GOING ITSELF: a purposeful trip, and a sortie with a stated objective.
branches.cn: 出行本身：一趟有目的的行程，以及一次有既定目标的出动。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE AND THEIR ROOM: a delegation abroad, and the building it works in.
branches.cn: 人与他们的房间：驻外代表团，以及它办公的馆舍。

branches.en: THE STATION: missionaries were sent, so their posting took the name of the sending.
branches.cn: 驻地：传教士被派出，因此驻地沿用了「派遣」之名。

branches.en: ONE ERRAND: the whole picture shrinks to a single afternoon's task.
branches.cn: 一件差事：整幅画面缩小到一个下午的任务。

intro.en: Mission is a Latin participle and action noun from the verb 'to send', and the same verb reaches several common English words.
intro.cn: mission 是由「发送」动词来的拉丁分词与动作名词，同一个动词还通向若干常用英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere gives mission, missile, dismiss, transmit and commission.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mittere 衍生 mission、missile（导弹）、dismiss（打发走）、transmit（传送）与 commission（委托）。

items.example: The root supplies the act of sending.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「发送」这个动作。

items.example: The participle supplies the miss- of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供词族里的 miss-。

items.example: The action noun is the direct source of mission.
items.exampleCN: 这个动作名词是 mission 的直接来源。

items.meaning: a task one is sent to do
items.example: The English word widened from sending to errand.
items.exampleCN: 英语词从「派遣」扩到「差事」。

items.meaning: one sent to spread a faith
items.example: The suffix marks the person sent.
The same root sends a weapon instead of a person.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根送出的是武器而不是人。

items.example: The prefix reverses the direction of sending.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把发送的方向反过来。

items.example: The prefix lengthens the road of the sending.
Entrusting is sending a task with authority.
items.exampleCN: 委托就是带着权力把任务送出去。

derivatives.zh: 传教士；传教的
委员会；委托
解散；解雇
传送；传播

definition_zh: 错误；过失；弄错；误认；误解
definition_en: a wrong act, decision or opinion, or the verb meaning to identify someone wrongly or to take words in the wrong sense
core_image: 手里拿着一把不属于自己的钥匙，插进锁孔却怎么也转不动
scene: 雨夜回家，楼道灯光昏暗，他把邻居的伞当成自己的拎了起来。In the dim hallway he mistook his neighbour's umbrella for his own and carried it home.
sceneCN: 这里是「把…误认成」（第 3 个义项：认错了对象）；句意为昏暗楼道里，他把邻居的伞当成了自己的，一路拎回家。图中可辨识物件：湿淋淋的伞、昏黄的楼道灯、住户门牌。

derivatives.zh: 由 mistake 的过去分词转作形容词，义为「弄错的；错误的」
由 mistaken 加 -ly 构成，义为「错误地」
由 un- 加 mistake 加 -able 构成，义为「不会认错的；明显的」

senses.title: A wrong judgement or act
senses.definition: an act or decision that is wrong, or an opinion that does not match the facts
senses.definitionCN: 做错的事、错误的决定，或与事实不符的看法
senses.example: Leaving the gas on all night was a dangerous mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 让煤气整夜开着，是个危险的错误。
senses.why: Old Norse mistaka joined mis-, wrongly, to taka, to take, so a mistake is literally a wrong taking; the noun keeps that picture of a hand closing on the wrong thing.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语 mistaka 由 mis-（错）加 taka（拿、取）构成，字面就是「拿错」；名词把这幅画面留着——手合拢时抓住的不是想要的那件东西，于是留下一个做错的结果。

senses.title: A small error in written or spoken form
senses.definition: a slip in spelling, punctuation, calculation or pronunciation rather than a fault of judgement
senses.definitionCN: 拼写、标点、计算或发音上的小失误，而不是判断上的过错
senses.example: The essay was good except for two spelling mistakes.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章写得不错，只是有两处拼写错误。
senses.why: A wrong grasp can be small as well as large: a hand that writes the wrong letter has still taken the wrong shape, so the same noun covers slips on paper and failures in life.
senses.whyCN: 「拿错」既可以很大，也可以很小：写字的手取了错误的字形，仍是拿错了东西；于是同一个名词既管纸上的笔误，也管生活里的过失。

senses.title: To take one person or thing for another
senses.definition: to believe that a person or thing is someone or something else, especially because they look similar
senses.definitionCN: 以为某人或某物是另一个人或另一件东西，尤因两者相像
senses.example: From the back of the hall she mistook me for my cousin.
senses.exampleCN: 在礼堂后排，她把我误认成了我表弟。
senses.why: Here the old compound is still visible: mis- says the taking is wrong, and the verb names the moment the eyes take one face and file it under another name.
senses.whyCN: 这里古诺斯语的构词还看得见：mis- 说明这一「取」取错了，动词命名的正是眼睛把一张脸拿了去、却归到另一个名字下的那一刻。

senses.title: To give someone's words the wrong meaning
senses.definition: to understand a remark or an intention in a way the speaker did not mean
senses.definitionCN: 把某句话或某种用意理解成说话人并未表达的意思
senses.example: Do not mistake my quietness for indifference.
senses.exampleCN: 别把我的沉默当成冷漠。
senses.why: The mind also takes: it receives words and stores a sense, and when the stored sense is not the one offered, English reuses the mis- plus take pattern and calls it a mistake of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 心智也在「取」：它接住话语、存下一个意思；存下的不是对方给出的那一个，英语便再次动用 mis- 加「取」的旧模式，把这叫意思上的拿错。

intro.en: Mistake came from a Norse compound of a prefix meaning wrongly and a verb meaning to take, and English first used it as a verb before it named the error itself.
intro.cn: mistake 来自古诺斯语中「表示错误的前缀＋表示拿取的动词」的复合体；英语先把它当动词用，后来才用它指错误本身。

items.en: The verb mistaka joined mis-, wrongly, to taka, to take, and meant to seize the wrong thing or to misjudge a matter.
items.cn: 动词 mistaka 把表示「错」的 mis- 与表示「拿」的 taka 合在一起，意为拿错了东西或把事情判断错了。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fourteenth century as mistaken, first in the sense of understanding a matter wrongly.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入这个动词，写作 mistaken，最早指把一件事理解错了。

items.en: A noun grew beside the verb, at first naming a wrong deed and later any small slip of hand or pen.
items.cn: 动词旁边长出一个名词，最初指做错的事，后来也指手上或笔下的任何小失误。

items.en: The phrase by mistake fixed the noun as the ordinary way of saying that something was done without intention.
items.cn: by mistake 这个说法把名词固定下来，成为表示「并非有意」的常用说法。

items.en: Modern English keeps the count noun and the verb alive and adds fixed patterns such as mistake A for B and a spelling mistake.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留可数名词与动词，并发展出 mistake A for B、a spelling mistake 这类固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same Norse stem through derived forms and the shared prefix; the near-meaning group gathers other words for going wrong.
note.cn: 形近组沿着同一个古诺斯语词干，收它的派生形式与共用的前缀；近义组收其他表示出错、走偏的词。

entries.definition: The past participle of mistake used as an adjective, meaning wrong in judgement or wrongly identified.
entries.definitionCN: mistake 的过去分词转作形容词，指判断有误或被误认的。

entries.definition: Built with un- and -able on mistake: too clear to be taken for anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 在 mistake 上加 un- 与 -able 构成，指清楚得不可能认错。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning wrongly, the element that turns a taking into a mistake.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「错误地」的前缀，正是它把一次「拿取」变成了拿错。

entries.definition: A wrong result or a departure from what is correct, often in calculation or judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 错误的结果或偏离正确之处，常用于计算或判断。

entries.definition: A careless and serious mistake, usually one that is embarrassing.
entries.definitionCN: 粗心而严重的错误，往往令人难堪。

entries.definition: A small mistake made by not paying attention.
entries.definitionCN: 因没留神而造成的小错。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a Norse verb of taking, and the whole family keeps the picture of a hand reaching for the wrong object.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从古诺斯语中一个「拿取」的动词开始，整个词族都留着伸手抓错东西的画面。

normal.en: The Norse verb was mis- plus taka, to take, so a mistake is first of all something taken wrongly.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语动词是 mis- 加 taka（拿），所以 mistake 首先是拿错了的东西。

normal.en: The same stem explains mistook and mistaken: one is the wrong take in the past, the other the state of having taken wrongly.
normal.cn: 同一词干也解释 mistook 与 mistaken：前者是过去的拿错，后者是已经拿错的状态。

normal.en: A spelling mistake is the smallest version of the picture: the hand takes the wrong letter.
normal.cn: spelling mistake 是这幅画最小的版本：手取错了字母。

normal.en: Mistake A for B puts two nouns on either side because the verb needs both the person seen and the name given.
normal.cn: mistake A for B 两边各放一个名词，因为动词既需要被看见的人，也需要被安上的名字。

normal.en: Mistakenly adds -ly, turning the error into the manner of an action.
normal.cn: mistakenly 加 -ly，把错误变成动作的方式。

abstract.en: A word built out of taking reminds us that most errors begin as a confident grab, not as doubt.
abstract.cn: 一个由「拿」造出的词提醒人：多数错误起于自信的一抓，而不是怀疑。

abstract.en: The distance between mistook and mistaken is the distance between doing and being: first the wrong grab, then the wrong state.
abstract.cn: mistook 与 mistaken 之间的距离，就是做与是的距离：先有错抓，再有错的状态。

abstract.en: In every mistake there is an intention that ran ahead of the facts.
abstract.cn: 每个 mistake 里都有一个跑在事实前面的意图。

examples.en: Everyone makes a mistake now and then.
examples.cn: 人偶尔都会犯错。

examples.en: He mistook the quiet street for a dead end.
examples.cn: 他把那条安静的街道误当成死胡同。

examples.en: A single spelling mistake can change the whole sentence.
examples.cn: 一个拼写错误就能改变整句话的意思。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷死忒克」——迷糊到极点就伸手拿错；记住 mistake 是弄错。

root: 古诺斯语 mistaka ＝ mis-（错）＋ taka（拿、取），本义「拿错、误取」，十四世纪进入英语。属北日耳曼语来源，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a wrong taking; from it grow the wrong act, the slip on paper, the misidentified person and the misread sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「拿错」；由此长出做错的事、纸上的小失误、认错的人以及听错的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing on the wrong object while the wanted one stays on the shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：手合拢时抓住的是一件错的东西，想要的那件还留在架上。

branches.en: a hand grabbing the wrong tool in a hurry
branches.cn: 匆忙中抓住了一件不顺手的工具

branches.en: a red circle around one letter on a page
branches.cn: 纸上一个字母被红笔圈住

branches.en: a stranger's umbrella taken in a dim hallway
branches.cn: 昏暗楼道里被拿走的陌生人的伞

branches.en: a kind remark heard as a cold one
branches.cn: 一句好意被听成了冷话

branches.en: a teacher counting errors before writing a comment
branches.cn: 老师先数错处再写评语

intro.en: The word is a Norse compound of a prefix and a verb of taking, carried into English noun and adjective forms by English endings.
intro.cn: 这个词是古诺斯语中「前缀＋拿取动词」的复合体，再靠英语词尾变成名词与形容词形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for mistake; the word belongs to the Norse side of Germanic, and the similar Latin capere is not its source.
latinIntro.cn: mistake 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它属于日耳曼语中的北支，形似的拉丁语 capere 并不是它的来源。

definition_zh: 混合；搅合；调配；交往；混合物
definition_en: to combine different things into one mass, to prepare something by blending ingredients, to spend time with others, or the blend itself
core_image: 两管不同颜色的颜料挤进同一只白碟，被勺子搅成一团新的颜色
scene: 画室的桌上摆着两管颜料，学生把颜色挤在同一只碟里。On the studio table the student squeezed two colours into one dish and began to mix them with a spoon.
sceneCN: 这里是「混合」（第 1 个义项：把不同东西搅在一起）；句意为学生把两种颜色挤进同一只碟子，用勺子开始搅。图中可辨识物件：两管颜料、白瓷碟、调色勺。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 mixt- 加 -ure 构成，义为「混合物」
由 mix 加 -er 构成，义为「搅拌器；调酒师」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「混合的；褒贬不一的」

senses.title: To combine separate things into one mass
senses.definition: to put different substances or things together and stir or blend them so that they form one whole
senses.definitionCN: 把不同的物质或东西放在一起搅动、拌合，使它们成为一个整体
senses.example: Mix the sand and cement before adding water.
senses.exampleCN: 加水和之前，先把沙与水泥搅拌在一起。
senses.why: Latin miscere meant to blend, and the word still begins with two things that were separate and are now folded into each other.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 miscere 意为混合；这个词的起点始终是两样原本分开的东西，此刻互相折了进去。

senses.title: To prepare something by blending ingredients
senses.definition: to make a drink, dough or other preparation by measuring and combining its parts
senses.definitionCN: 按分量把各组成部分合在一起，做出饮料、面团或其他制品
senses.example: She mixed a bowl of batter for the pancakes.
senses.exampleCN: 她调了一碗做薄饼的面糊。
senses.why: Once blending is a deliberate act, it can serve a recipe: the cook measures first and folds second, so the same verb covers both the stirring and the thing being made.
senses.whyCN: 当混合成了一种有意的动作，它就可以为一份食谱服务：先量、后拌；于是同一个动词既管搅动，也管做出来的东西。

senses.title: To spend time and talk with other people
senses.definition: to be with other people socially, especially at a gathering
senses.definitionCN: 在社交场合与他人相处、交谈，尤指在聚会上
senses.example: At the reception he mixed easily with guests he had never met.
senses.exampleCN: 招待会上，他和从未见过的客人也能自在地交谈。
senses.why: People in a room are separate individuals until conversation folds them into a group; the social sense borrows exactly that picture of separate units becoming one gathering.
senses.whyCN: 满屋子的人原本是一个个分开的个体，谈话把他们折进同一个群体；社交义借的正是「分开的单位合成一个场合」这幅画。

senses.title: A blend, or a packet of ready-measured ingredients
senses.definition: a combination of different things, or a commercial packet in which the dry parts of a recipe are already combined
senses.definitionCN: 不同东西的组合，或商店里把一份食谱的干料预先配好的包装
senses.example: The stall sells a soup mix that needs only hot water.
senses.exampleCN: 那个摊位卖一种汤料包，只需加热水。
senses.why: When the verb's result is treated as a thing, it becomes a noun: whatever came out of the bowl, or the packet that saves the cook the measuring.
senses.whyCN: 当动词的结果被当成一件东西，它就变成名词：可以是碗里拌出来的成品，也可以是替厨师省去称量的那袋配料。

intro.en: Mix goes back through Latin miscere and its participle mixtus; English first used mixt as an adjective and later formed the short verb mix from it.
intro.cn: mix 经由拉丁语 miscere 及其分词 mixtus 而来；英语先用 mixt 作形容词，后来又从它反推出简短动词 mix。

items.en: Miscere meant to mix or blend, and it supplied the participle that carried the idea into several European languages.
items.cn: miscere 意为混合、拌合，它提供的分词把这一概念送进了欧洲的好几种语言。

items.en: The past participle mixtus described something already blended, and Old French kept a form of it as mixte.
items.cn: 过去分词 mixtus 描述已经混好的东西，古法语保留了它的一个形式 mixte。

items.en: English used mixt as an adjective and participle for a blended substance, following the French form rather than the Latin spelling.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语用 mixt 作形容词与分词，指已经混合的物质，拼写跟着法语而不是拉丁语。

items.en: A short verb mix was formed from mixt by dropping the final t, and the first records are generally dated to the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 简短的动词 mix 一般认为是在十六世纪由 mixt 去掉词尾的 t 反推而成，最早的记录也定在这个世纪。

items.en: The verb spread into cooking, chemistry and music, while the noun mix named both the blend and the packet of measured dry ingredients.
items.cn: 这个动词扩展到烹饪、化学与音乐；名词 mix 既指混好的东西，也指配好分量的干料包。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin-derived relatives and the English derivatives; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of joining substances or people.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁来源的同族词与英语派生词；近义组收表示把物质或人合到一起的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a blended result, built on the Latin stem mixt- with -ure.
entries.definitionCN: 表示混合结果的名词，由拉丁词干 mixt- 加 -ure 构成。

entries.definition: A machine or a person that mixes, formed by adding -er to the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 搅拌的机器或人，由动词加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective, meaning blended or of more than one kind.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词转作形容词，指混合的，或由不止一种构成的。

entries.definition: To mix things so smoothly that the parts are no longer easy to tell apart.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西混得十分均匀，以致不易分辨各组成部分。

entries.definition: To bring two or more things together, often while each keeps its own identity.
entries.definitionCN: 把两样或更多东西合在一起，往往各自仍保留特性。

entries.definition: To mix with people at a gathering, or for things to flow together.
entries.definitionCN: 在聚会上与人交往，或指事物交融在一起。

normalIntro.en: The word comes from a Latin verb of blending, and its family keeps returning to the moment separate parts lose their edges.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语中表示混合的动词，同族词反复回到「分开的部分失去边界」的那一刻。

normal.en: Miscere is the Latin verb for blending, and mixture keeps its stem mixt- in plain view.
normal.cn: miscere 是拉丁语中表示混合的动词，mixture 把它的词干 mixt- 明明白白保留着。

normal.en: Mix was clipped from mixt, an older participle, so the verb is younger than the adjective it came from.
normal.cn: mix 是从较早的分词 mixt 截短而来，所以这个动词比它所出的形容词更年轻。

normal.en: A cake mix is the recipe before the cook: the dry parts are already combined in the packet.
normal.cn: cake mix 是厨师动手之前的食谱：干料已经在袋子里配好了。

normal.en: Mix with people uses the social sense of the same picture: separate persons folded into one gathering.
normal.cn: mix with people 用的是同一幅画的社会义：分开的人被折进同一个场合。

normal.en: Mixed feelings are feelings of more than one kind stirred together, which is the adjective's everyday life.
normal.cn: mixed feelings 是两种以上情绪搅在一起，正是这个形容词的日常用法。

abstract.en: Nothing in the word says the parts must disappear, only that they now share one space.
abstract.cn: 这个词没有说各部分必须消失，只说他共享了同一个空间。

abstract.en: Cooking, chemistry and conversation all use the same verb because all three are about boundaries giving way.
abstract.cn: 烹饪、化学与交谈都用同一个动词，因为三者都在说边界让开。

abstract.en: A mixture is a small argument for the value of difference: the result is neither part alone.
abstract.cn: 混合物是差异之价值的一个小小论据：结果既不是原来的任何一方。

examples.en: Mix the flour and water until the dough is smooth.
examples.cn: 把面粉和水混合，直到面团变得光滑。

examples.en: He mixed a little lime juice into the drink.
examples.cn: 他在饮料里调进了一点青柠汁。

examples.en: She finds it hard to mix with strangers at parties.
examples.cn: 她觉得在聚会上很难与陌生人打交道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米克斯」——把米和克都倒进一只碗里搅匀，就是混合。

root: 一般认为由拉丁语 miscere（混合）的过去分词 mixtus，经中古英语 mixt 反推成动词 mix；同族有 mixture、mixer、mixed。

sensesIntro.en: Blending two things is the core; the senses move to cooking a recipe, to people folding into a group, and finally to the blend or packet as a thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 把两样东西混在一起是核心；义项走向按食谱调配，走向人合成一个场合，最后走向作为成品的混合物或配料包。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two colours squeezed into one white dish and stirred into a third colour.
core.cn: 核心意象：两管颜色挤进同一只白碟，被搅成第三种颜色。

branches.en: two colours folding into each other on a palette
branches.cn: 调色板上互相折进去的两种颜色

branches.en: a bowl of batter waiting beside a hot pan
branches.cn: 热锅旁等着下锅的一碗面糊

branches.en: a guest moving between small groups at a party
branches.cn: 晚会上在人群之间走动的客人

branches.en: a shelf of soup packets filled with dry ingredients
branches.cn: 货架上装着干配料的汤料包

branches.en: a factory line filling packets with pre-blended powder
branches.cn: 工厂流水线把预混好的粉末装进袋子

intro.en: A Latin verb of blending, its participle, and English endings that build the noun, the device and the past form carry the word.
intro.cn: 一个表示混合的拉丁动词、它的分词，以及造出名词、器具名与过去形式的英语词尾，共同撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: Mix has a secure Latin ancestry through miscere and its participle mixtus, which is why several related forms share the mixt- stem.
latinIntro.cn: mix 经由 miscere 及其分词 mixtus 有可靠的拉丁来源，所以好几个相关形式共用 mixt- 这个词干。

items.meaning: a device or person that mixes

definition_zh: 混合物；混合；混合料；交织的情感
definition_en: a combination of different things; also the act of combining them, a prepared blend, and a mingling of feelings
core_image: 一只碗里倒进面粉、水与糖，几样东西被搅成一体，分不清彼此
scene: 厨房的台面上摊着面粉、鸡蛋和牛奶，一只手把碗里的东西搅得越来越匀。With a few quick strokes, the mixture in the bowl became smooth and pale.
sceneCN: 这里是「混合物、搅好的东西」（第 1 个义项：由不同成分合在一起的整体）；句意为搅了几下，碗里的混合物就变得细腻发白。图中可辨识物件：面碗、木勺、散落的面粉。

pos.zh: 混合物；混合；混合料；交织的情感

derivatives.zh: 与 mixture 同出拉丁语 miscere（混合），经中古英语 mixen 简化为动词，义为「混合」
由 mix 加表示「做某事的工具或人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「搅拌器；调音台」
由 mix 加 -ing 构成，义为「混合；混音」
由 ad-（附加）加拉丁语 mixtura 构成，义为「掺入物；附加成分」

senses.title: A combination of different substances
senses.definition: something made by putting two or more different substances or things together
senses.definitionCN: 两种或更多不同物质合在一起形成的东西
senses.example: Stir the mixture until the sugar dissolves.
senses.exampleCN: 把混合物搅拌到糖完全溶解。
senses.why: Latin mixtura named the result of miscere, the act of stirring things together, so the noun was born pointing at the finished blend rather than at the stirring.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mixtura 指 miscere（把东西搅到一起）的结果，所以这个名词从一开始就指搅好的成品，而不是指搅这个动作。

senses.title: The act of bringing things together
senses.definition: the process of putting different things together so that they combine
senses.definitionCN: 把不同东西放到一起使它们合成一体的过程
senses.example: The recipe calls for a slow mixture of butter and flour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个配方要求把黄油与面粉慢慢地混合。
senses.why: The same Latin stem could name the deed as well as its result, and English kept both, so one word covers the stirring and the thing stirred.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁词干既能指动作，也能指动作的结果，英语把两者都留了下来，于是一个词既管搅拌这个动作，也管搅出来的东西。

senses.title: A blend prepared for cooking or medicine
senses.definition: a combination of ingredients prepared for a particular purpose, especially in baking or as a medicine
senses.definitionCN: 为某个具体用途按配方调好的多种成分，尤用于烘焙或作药
senses.example: The chemist measured a cough mixture into a small brown bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 药剂师把止咳药水量进一只棕色小瓶。
senses.why: From blends in general the word narrowed to blends made for a use: flour and eggs for a cake, drugs and syrup for a cough, each following its own recipe.
senses.whyCN: 从泛指的混合物，词义收窄到为某个用途调配的混合物：做蛋糕的面粉鸡蛋、治咳嗽的药与糖浆，各自按自己的配方来。

senses.title: A mingling of feelings
senses.definition: a combination of different feelings or qualities that appear together
senses.definitionCN: 不同情感或特质同时出现、彼此掺杂的状态
senses.example: She spoke with a mixture of relief and regret.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话时带着宽慰与懊悔交织的心情。
senses.why: A blend does not have to be physical: once the word meant any combined whole, it could hold invisible ingredients such as relief and regret in one sentence.
senses.whyCN: 混合物不必是实物：当这个词可以泛指任何合成的整体，它就能在同一句里装下宽慰与懊悔这些看不见的成分。

intro.en: Mixture comes from Latin mixtura, a noun of result built on the verb miscere, and it entered English through French with the sense of a blended whole.
intro.cn: mixture 来自拉丁语 mixtura，这个名词由动词 miscere 的「结果」义构成，经法语进入英语，意为混合成的整体。

items.en: Miscere meant to mix, stir or mingle, and it described liquids as well as, figuratively, people and affairs.
items.cn: miscere 意为混合、搅动、掺在一起，既用于液体，也比喻用于人和事务。

items.en: Its past participle mixtus meant having been mixed, and that form supplied the stem for the nouns built on the result.
items.cn: 它的过去分词 mixtus 意为「已被混合的」，为后来表示结果的各名词提供了词干。

items.en: Mixtura added the noun suffix -tura to the participle stem and named the thing produced by mixing.
items.cn: mixtura 在分词词干后加名词后缀 -tura，指混合之后产生的东西。

items.en: Old French took the noun as mixture and passed it into English in the fourteenth century alongside learned borrowings from Latin.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词作 mixture，在十四世纪随拉丁语借词一起传入英语。

items.en: English widened mixture from substances to recipes and medicines, then to feelings and qualities that appear together.
items.cn: 英语把 mixture 从物质扩展到配方与药水，再扩展到同时出现的情感与特质。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the Latin verb of mixing; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for combined wholes in chemistry, cooking and everyday speech.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「混合」动词的同族词；近义组收化学、烹饪与日常说法里表示合成整体的名词。

entries.definition: To put different things together so that they form one mass.
entries.definitionCN: 把不同东西放在一起，使它们成为一体。

entries.definition: A machine or device that stirs ingredients together.
entries.definitionCN: 把原料搅在一起的机器或器具。

entries.definition: Something added to a main substance in a smaller amount.
entries.definitionCN: 以较少分量掺入主要物质的东西。

entries.definition: An old adjective meaning mixed, now replaced by mixed in ordinary use.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧的形容词，意为混合的，日常已由 mixed 取代。

entries.definition: A mixture of two or more things that go well together.
entries.definitionCN: 两种或更多彼此协调的东西混合成的整体。

entries.definition: A substance formed from two or more elements or parts.
entries.definitionCN: 由两种或更多成分构成的物质。

entries.definition: A metal made by melting two or more metals together.
entries.definitionCN: 把两种或更多金属熔在一起制成的金属。

entries.definition: The result of joining separate things into one arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 把分开的事物合成一种安排的结果。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb of stirring, and its family keeps returning to the act of mixing and to the thing that mixing leaves behind.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语「搅拌」动词上，同族词反复回到搅拌这个动作，以及搅拌之后留下的东西。

normal.en: Miscere in Latin means to mix, so mixture rests on the act of stirring, not on any single ingredient.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 miscere 意为混合，所以 mixture 依托的是「搅」这个动作，而不是某一种原料。

normal.en: -tura is a Latin noun ending for the result of an action, so mixtura is literally the thing that mixing leaves behind.
normal.cn: -tura 是拉丁语里表示动作结果的名词词尾，所以 mixtura 字面就是「搅拌之后留下的东西」。

normal.en: Mix, mixer and admixture share the same stem, which is why one Latin verb yields a verb, a tool and an added element.
normal.cn: mix、mixer 与 admixture 共用同一个词干，所以一个拉丁动词能长出动词、工具和掺入物三种词。

normal.en: A cough mixture and a cake mixture follow one pattern: a list of ingredients turned into something usable.
normal.cn: 止咳药水和蛋糕面糊是同一个路子：一张配料清单变成一样可用的东西。

normal.en: A mixture of relief and regret shows that the word needs no physical ingredients, since feelings can be blended too.
normal.cn: 「宽慰与懊悔的混合」说明这个词不必有实物成分，情感也能被搅在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl where flour, water and sugar lose their outlines and become one pale mass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗，面粉、水与糖各自失去轮廓，变成一整团浅色的东西。

abstract.en: Every mixture keeps traces of its parts: you can still taste each ingredient after they merge.
abstract.cn: 每个混合物都留着各成分的痕迹：合成一体之后，仍能尝出每一种原料。

abstract.en: A word born from stirring shows that English often names a whole by the action that produced it.
abstract.cn: 一个从「搅」里出生的词说明，英语常用产生整体的那个动作来给整体命名。

examples.en: Stir the mixture until the sugar dissolves.
examples.cn: 把混合物搅拌到糖完全溶解。

examples.en: She spoke with a mixture of relief and regret.
examples.cn: 她说话时带着宽慰与懊悔交织的心情。

examples.en: The pharmacist shook the bottle before pouring the mixture.
examples.cn: 药剂师倒药水之前先摇了摇瓶子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米克斯扯」——几样东西被米克在一起，扯也扯不开；记住 mixture 是混合物，也可指药水与心情的掺杂。

root: 拉丁语 miscere（混合）的过去分词 mixtus 加名词后缀 -tura 构成 mixtura（混合物），经古法语 mixture 进入英语；同族词有 mix、mixer、admixture。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a blended whole; the senses divide into the act of mixing, the prepared recipe, and the mingling of feelings.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是混合成的整体；义项由此分出搅拌的动作、按配方调好的混合料，以及情感的交织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl in which separate ingredients lose their outlines and become one mass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只碗，几样分开的原料在其中失去轮廓，合成一团。

branches.en: a bowl of batter turning smooth under a spoon
branches.cn: 木勺搅动下渐渐变细的面糊

branches.en: two hands folding one powder into another
branches.cn: 两只手把一种粉末折进另一种里

branches.en: a labelled bottle of cough syrup on a shelf
branches.cn: 货架上一瓶贴了标签的止咳糖浆

branches.en: one face showing relief and regret at the same time
branches.cn: 同一张脸上宽慰与懊悔并存

branches.en: the same noun serving a kitchen bowl and a chemist's bottle
branches.cn: 同一个名词，一次指厨房的碗，一次指药房的瓶子

intro.en: A Latin verb of stirring, its participle, a noun ending of result and four English forms carry the word from the bowl to the pharmacy.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「搅拌」动词、它的分词、一个表示结果的名词词尾，再加上四个英语形式，把这个词从碗带到了药房。

latinIntro.en: Latin miscere, mixtus and mixtura form a tight family of mixing words, and English borrowed all three links.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 miscere、mixtus 与 mixtura 构成一个紧密的「混合」词族，英语把这三个环节都借了过来。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作结果的名词词尾

definition_zh: 可移动的；流动的；手机；活动雕塑
definition_en: able to move or be moved; changing place or rank easily; also a phone carried by the user and a hanging sculpture turned by air
core_image: 一只箱子装上小轮，人一推就走，位置随时能换
scene: 夜里的车站出口挤满人，一个年轻人拖着箱子，另一只手举着小屏幕贴在耳边。She answered her mobile while dragging a suitcase through the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里是「手机」（第 3 个义项：随身携带的移动电话）；句意为她一边拖着行李箱穿过人群，一边接听手机。图中可辨识物件：滚轮行李箱、亮着的屏幕、车站出口的灯。

pos.zh: 可移动的；流动的；变动灵活的

derivatives.zh: 由 mobile 去 e 加 -ity 构成，义为「流动性；移动能力」
由 mobile 加 -ize 构成，义为「动员；组织起来行动」
由希腊语 autos（自己）加 mobile（可动的）构成，义为「汽车」
由否定前缀 im- 加 mobile 构成，义为「不能移动的；静止的」

senses.title: Able to move or be moved
senses.definition: able to move by itself, or able to be moved from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 能自行移动，或能被从一个地方搬到另一个地方
senses.example: A mobile desk lets you work in either room.
senses.exampleCN: 一张可移动的书桌让你在哪个房间都能工作。
senses.why: Latin mobilis was built from movere, to move, plus -bilis, able to be, so the adjective literally says able to move before it ever says anything about phones.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mobilis 由 movere（移动）加 -bilis（能……的）构成，所以这个形容词字面上先说「能动」，比它用来指手机要早得多。

senses.title: Changing place or rank easily
senses.definition: able or likely to change job, home or social position
senses.definitionCN: 能够或容易更换工作、住所或社会地位的
senses.example: A mobile workforce follows the work wherever it appears.
senses.exampleCN: 流动的劳动力会跟着工作机会走。
senses.why: If a thing can be moved, people and jobs can move too, so English extended the same adjective to labour, to families and to whole societies that do not stay put.
senses.whyCN: 如果一样东西能被搬动，人和工作也能移动，于是英语把这同一个形容词扩展到劳动力、家庭乃至不断变动的社会。

senses.title: A telephone carried with you
senses.definition: a telephone that works through a network of radio cells and is carried by its user
senses.definitionCN: 依靠蜂窝式无线电网络工作、由使用者随身携带的电话
senses.example: She answered her mobile while dragging a suitcase through the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 她一边拖着行李箱穿过人群，一边接听手机。
senses.why: A phone that is not tied to a desk or a wall socket inherits the oldest sense of the adjective, and English simply dropped the noun phone and kept the describing word.
senses.whyCN: 不拴在桌上或墙上的电话继承了形容词最老的意思；英语省掉了 phone 这个名词，只留下那个起描述作用的词。

senses.title: A hanging sculpture turned by air
senses.definition: a sculpture of balanced parts that hang and turn with air currents
senses.definitionCN: 由平衡的部件悬挂而成、随气流转动的雕塑
senses.example: A metal mobile turned slowly above the hospital bed.
senses.exampleCN: 一件金属活动雕塑在病床上方缓缓转动。
senses.why: Alexander Calder made hanging works whose parts shift with the slightest breath, and the ready-made word for anything movable was borrowed to name the genre.
senses.whyCN: 雕塑家考尔德做了许多悬挂作品，部件随最轻的气流改变位置，于是那个现成的「可动之物」被借来给这类作品命名。

intro.en: Mobile is Latin mobilis, able to move, built on the verb movere, and English took it through French before applying it to phones and to hanging sculptures.
intro.cn: mobile 是拉丁语 mobilis（能移动的），由动词 movere（移动）构成；英语经法语借入，后来才用于手机与悬挂雕塑。

items.en: Movere meant to move, to set in motion or to stir, and it stands behind a large family of English words about motion.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、使动起来、搅动，英语里一大族与运动有关的词都出自它。

items.en: The suffix -bilis turned a verb into an adjective of possibility, so movere plus -bilis gave a word for what can be moved.
items.cn: 后缀 -bilis 把动词变成表示可能性的形容词，于是 movere 加 -bilis 就得出了「能被移动的」这个词。

items.en: Mobilis meant movable and also changeable, and it already described unsettled people and shifting fortune, not only objects.
items.cn: mobilis 既指可移动的，也指易变的，它早就不只用于实物，还用来描述不安定的人和变动不居的命运。

items.en: Old French kept the adjective as mobile, and English borrowed it in the fifteenth century, first in the language of law and natural philosophy.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词保留为 mobile，英语在十五世纪借入，最早用在法律与自然哲学的语言里。

items.en: Modern English added the telephone sense in the late twentieth century and the hanging-sculpture sense in the nineteen thirties, both resting on the same idea of easy movement.
items.cn: 现代英语在二十世纪后期加上了电话义，在一九三〇年代加上了悬挂雕塑义，两者都建立在「容易移动」这一同一个想法上。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb of moving and its adjective; the near-meaning group gathers words for things light enough or free enough to be carried about.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语「移动」动词及其形容词展开；近义组收表示「轻便得可以随身带走」的词。

entries.definition: The ability to move or to change position or job.
entries.definitionCN: 移动或更换位置、工作的能力。

entries.definition: A car, literally a self-moving vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 汽车，字面是「自己会动的交通工具」。

entries.definition: Unable to move; fixed in place.
entries.definitionCN: 不能移动的；固定在一处的。

entries.definition: To organize people or resources so that they can act.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或资源组织起来以便行动。

entries.definition: Light and small enough to carry with you.
entries.definitionCN: 轻小便携、可以随身携带的。

entries.definition: Able to be shifted from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 能从一处移到另一处的。

entries.definition: Able to be carried or shipped from place to place.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被运来运去的。

entries.definition: Small enough to hold and use in the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 小到可以握在手里使用的。

normalIntro.en: The word descends from the Latin verb to move, and its family keeps splitting into what can be shifted, who can move up, and the device that travels with a person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语「移动」的动词，同族词不断分成三类：能被挪动的东西、能向上流动的人，以及跟着人走的设备。

normal.en: Movere is the Latin verb to move, and its family spreads across English in mobile, motion, motor, remove and promote.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」的动词，它的词族铺满英语，见于 mobile、motion、motor、remove 与 promote。

normal.en: -bilis marks what can be done, so mobilis is not merely moving but movable, and immobile is its negated twin.
normal.cn: -bilis 标记「可以做到的」，所以 mobilis 不只是「动」，而是「可被移动」；immobile 则是它的否定对应。

normal.en: The noun dropped phone and kept the adjective: a mobile is a telephone defined by its freedom from a fixed line.
normal.cn: 名词省掉了 phone，只留下形容词：a mobile 就是靠「不拴在固定线路上」来定义的一部电话。

normal.en: Mobility adds -ity to mobile and turns the ability to move into a measurable social fact.
normal.cn: mobility 在 mobile 后加 -ity，把「能移动」变成一项可以衡量的社会事实。

normal.en: Calder's hanging works were called mobiles because they move, a young sense resting on the oldest core of the word.
normal.cn: 考尔德的悬挂作品被称为 mobile，因为它们会动；这个年轻的义项仍立足于这个词最老的核心。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase with wheels: the same object stays whole while its place keeps changing.
abstract.cn: 想象一只带轮子的箱子：东西还是那件东西，位置却一直在换。

abstract.en: A word for easy movement ends up naming a phone, a workforce and a work of art, because all three refuse to stay fixed.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「容易移动」的词最后指手机、劳动力和一件艺术品，因为这三者都不肯固定不动。

abstract.en: What can be moved can also be re-ranked, so physical mobility quietly turns into social mobility.
abstract.cn: 能被搬动的东西也能被重新排位，于是身体的移动悄悄变成了社会地位的流动。

examples.en: A mobile desk lets you work in either room.
examples.cn: 一张可移动的书桌让你在哪个房间都能工作。

examples.en: She answered her mobile while dragging a suitcase through the crowd.
examples.cn: 她一边拖着行李箱穿过人群，一边接听手机。

examples.en: The gallery hung a large mobile above the stairs.
examples.cn: 画廊在楼梯上方挂了一件大型活动雕塑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「谋拜偶」——举着手机四处谋生，走到哪儿拜到哪儿；记住 mobile 是可移动的，也指手机与活动雕塑。

root: 拉丁语 movere（移动）加后缀 -bilis（能……的）构成 mobilis（可移动的），经古法语 mobile 进入英语；同族词有 mobility、mobilize、automobile、immobile。

sensesIntro.en: The core is easy movement; the senses divide into things that can be shifted, people who change rank, the phone in a pocket, and the sculpture that turns in the air.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「容易移动」；义项由此分出能被挪动的东西、能换地位的人、口袋里的手机，以及在空中转动的雕塑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wheeled case that stays whole while its place keeps changing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只带轮子的箱子，东西不变，位置一直在换。

branches.en: a desk pushed from one room into another
branches.cn: 一张书桌被从一间房推到另一间房

branches.en: a family packing up for a job in a new city
branches.cn: 一家人为了新城市的工作打包搬家

branches.en: a handset lifted to an ear on a crowded platform
branches.cn: 拥挤站台上举到耳边的一部手机

branches.en: metal arms turning slowly above a bed
branches.cn: 病床上方缓缓转动的金属臂

branches.en: one word for the worker who moves and the phone that moves with him
branches.cn: 同一个词，既指流动的工人，也指跟着他走的手机

intro.en: A Latin verb of moving and its possibility suffix supply the stem, while four English forms carry the word to phones, sculpture and social rank.
intro.cn: 拉丁语「移动」动词与表示可能性的后缀提供词干，四个英语形式再把这个词带向手机、雕塑与社会地位。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere and its adjective mobilis supply the whole family, while motus and motor name the movement and the one who moves.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 movere 及其形容词 mobilis 支撑起整个词族，motus 与 motor 则分别指运动与推动者。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾

definition_zh: 方式；模式；交通方式；生产方式；时尚；调式；语气；众数
definition_en: a way in which something is done, operates, or exists; also a prevailing fashion, a musical scale, a grammatical mood, or the most frequent value in a set
core_image: 一把尺子量出恰好的一段，再照这个尺寸去做
scene: 出行方案表里列了地铁、公交、骑车和步行四种方式，让人比较城市负担得起哪一种。The transport plan lists four modes — metro, bus, bicycle and walking — and asks which one the city can afford.
sceneCN: 这里 mode 是「交通方式」（第 3 个义项：交通方式）；句意：这份交通规划列出四种方式——地铁、公交、自行车和步行——并追问这座城市负担得起哪一种。场景要点：一张摊开的城市交通图、四条并排的路线、被圈出的预算数字；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 方式；模式；样式；调式；语气；众数

derivatives.zh: 形式的；模态的；语气的
形式；模态；感觉通道

senses.title: A way of doing
senses.definition: the particular way in which someone does something or something happens
senses.definitionCN: 某人做某事或某事发生的特定方式
senses.example: Her mode of working is to write everything by hand before typing it.
senses.exampleCN: 她的工作方式是先把一切手写下来，再打字。
senses.why: Latin modus is a measure. A way of doing something is the measure the action is cut to, so the word begins as the shape given to an activity rather than its purpose.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modus 是“尺度”。做某事的方式，就是动作被裁成的尺寸，因此这个词的起点是给一项活动定形，而不是给它定目的。

senses.title: A machine setting
senses.definition: one of the fixed settings in which a machine or system can operate
senses.definitionCN: 机器或系统可以运行的固定设置之一
senses.example: At ten the alarm switches itself into night mode.
senses.exampleCN: 到了十点，警报器会自动切换到夜间模式。
senses.why: A machine repeats the same operations, and each setting is a measure it can be set to. The word moves from human ways of acting to the repeatable ways a device acts.
senses.whyCN: 机器重复同样的操作，每一种设置都是它可以被调到的某个尺度。这个词从人的行事方式，转到设备可重复的运行方式。

senses.title: A way to travel
senses.definition: a particular means or system of moving people or goods, such as rail, road, air, or water
senses.definitionCN: 运送人或货物的特定手段或系统，如铁路、公路、航空或水运
senses.example: Rail is still the cheapest mode of transport for coal.
senses.exampleCN: 对煤炭来说，铁路仍是最便宜的运输方式。
senses.why: Transport is measured out by the vehicle and the route chosen. The fixed phrase 'mode of transport' treats each means of travel as one measured option among several.
senses.whyCN: 运输由所选的交通工具与路线量定。固定短语“mode of transport”把每一种出行手段都当作若干被量定的选项之一。

senses.title: A way of producing
senses.definition: the organized way in which a society or economy makes goods, especially in economic and historical writing
senses.definitionCN: 社会或经济制造商品的有机组织方式，尤用于经济与历史写作
senses.example: The factory changed the mode of production from batch work to a moving line.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把生产方式从分批作业改成了流水线。
senses.why: Economics borrowed the measure for the whole arrangement of work: tools, labour, and ownership fitted together into one measured pattern of making things.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借用了这个“尺度”，用来指整个劳动安排：工具、劳动力与所有权被合成一个被量定的制造格局。

senses.title: The prevailing fashion
senses.definition: the current fashion or style, especially in dress, in somewhat formal or old-fashioned use
senses.definitionCN: 当下的风尚或款式，尤指服饰，语气较正式或略显旧式
senses.example: Narrow coats were the mode in the winter of that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天，窄身大衣正是风尚。
senses.why: French mode means fashion, a specialized use of the same word. Fashion is the measure everyone agrees to wear for a season, so the sense of 'current style' grows straight out of 'measure'.
senses.whyCN: 法语 mode 意为“时尚”，是同一个词的专门用法。时尚就是大家在一季里共同同意穿着的尺度，所以“当下款式”这一义项直接从“尺度”长出来。

senses.title: A musical mode
senses.definition: a pattern of intervals used to organize a melody, especially one of the ancient or church modes
senses.definitionCN: 用来组织旋律的音程模式，尤指古代调式或教会调式
senses.example: The second movement is built on an old church mode rather than a major key.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章建立在古老的教会调式上，而不是大调上。
senses.why: Latin modus also meant rhythm and song. Musicians divide the octave by a measured pattern, and that pattern of intervals is literally the measure of the melody.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modus 也指节奏与歌曲。音乐家按一种被量定的模式划分八度，这种音程模式字面上就是旋律的尺度。

senses.title: A grammatical mood
senses.definition: the form of a verb that shows whether it states, commands, wishes, or supposes
senses.definitionCN: 动词的形式，表明它是在陈述、命令、祝愿还是假设
senses.example: In Latin the verb's mode tells whether it states a fact or gives an order.
senses.exampleCN: 在拉丁语中，动词的语气表明它是在陈述事实还是下达命令。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word for the form that measures the speaker's attitude toward the action. Late Latin used modus for this category, and English kept it beside the more common 'mood'.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借用了这个词，指量定说话人对动作态度的形式。晚期拉丁语用 modus 指这一范畴，英语把它与更常见的 mood 并留着。

senses.title: The statistical mode
senses.definition: in statistics, the value that occurs most frequently in a set of data
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中在一组数据里出现次数最多的值
senses.example: In this data set the mode is 4, because 4 appears more often than any other value.
senses.exampleCN: 在这组数据中，众数是 4，因为 4 出现的次数比其他任何值都多。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the old sense of measure but points it at frequency: the mode is the value where the data pile up, the measure at which the set is most itself.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留了这个词古老的“尺度”义，却把它指向频次：众数是数据堆积之处，是这组数据最像自己的那个尺度。

senses.title: A whole way of being
senses.definition: a general state or manner of existence, as in 'survival mode' or 'a mode of life'
senses.definitionCN: 总体的存在状态或生活方式，如“survival mode”或“a mode of life”
senses.example: During the storm the crew went into survival mode and stopped all repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨期间，船员进入求生模式，停止了所有修理。
senses.why: The measure can be applied to a whole life, not just one action. A mode of being is the overall pattern a person or group is currently cut to.
senses.whyCN: 这个尺度可以被用在整整一种生活上，而不只是一个动作。存在方式，就是一个人或群体当下被裁成的总体格局。

intro.en: Mode comes from Latin modus 'measure' through French, and the same measure runs through music, grammar, fashion, economics, and statistics. Its look-alike mood is a different word. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mode 经法语来自拉丁语 modus“尺度”，同一把尺子贯穿音乐、语法、时尚、经济与统计。与它形近的 mood 是另一个词。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Mode is first recorded in English meaning 'melodies, strains of music', a sense now obsolete. It came from Old French mode and directly from Latin modus.
items.cn: mode 在英语中最早记录为“旋律、乐曲”，这一义项今已废弃。它来自古法语 mode，并直接来自拉丁语 modus。

items.en: Latin modus meant 'measure, extent, quantity; proper measure, rhythm, song; a way, manner, fashion, style', and in Late Latin also 'mood' in grammar and logic.
items.cn: 拉丁语 modus 意为“尺度、范围、数量；恰当的尺度、节奏、歌曲；方式、做法、样式、风格”，在晚期拉丁语中还指语法与逻辑中的“语气”。

items.en: Modus goes back to PIE *med- 'take appropriate measures'. The same root lies behind moderate, modest, modify, model, modern, and medicine.
items.cn: modus 可追溯到原始印欧语 *med-“采取恰当的尺度”。同一词根也是 moderate、modest、modify、model、modern、medicine 的来源。

items.en: A second French borrowing gives mode the sense 'current fashion, prevailing style' (1640s). The central sense 'manner of acting or doing, the way in which a thing is done' is recorded by the 1660s.
items.cn: 另一次法语借入使 mode 获得“当下时尚、流行款式”之义（17 世纪 40 年代）。核心义“行事方式、做一件事的方式”到 17 世纪 60 年代才有记录。

items.en: The grammatical sense 'inflectional category in conjugation' is mid-15c. In music, mode is recorded from the 1670s for the Greek method of dividing the octave, and by 1721 for modern music.
items.cn: 语法义“变位中的屈折范畴”出现于 15 世纪中叶。音乐中，mode 于 17 世纪 70 年代指希腊人划分八度的方法，到 1721 年指现代音乐中的调式。

items.en: Mood 'state of mind' (c. 1300) comes from Old English mod 'heart, frame of mind', a word of unknown origin, and has no etymological link with mode. Grammatical mood (1570s) is a different word again: it is an alteration of mode.
items.cn: mood“心境”（约 1300）来自古英语 mod“心、心境”，词源不明，与 mode 没有词源关系。语法上的 mood（16 世纪 70 年代）又是另一个词：它是 mode 的变体拼写。

note.en: The first group separates mode from the look-alikes built on the same or a neighbouring stem; the second compares the ordinary words for 'the way something is done'.
note.cn: 第一组把 mode 与同词干或邻近词干的形近词分开；第二组比较表示“做事的方式”的常用词。

entries.tag: state of mind, not from modus
entries.definition: a temporary state of mind or feeling. It comes from Old English mod, not from Latin modus. Only the grammatical mood is a different word, an alteration of mode.
entries.definitionCN: 暂时的心境或情绪。它来自古英语 mod，而不是拉丁语 modus。只有语法上的 mood 是另一个词，即 mode 的变体。

entries.definition: a small representation or an example to copy. It goes back to Latin modellus, a diminutive of modus, so it is 'a little measure' rather than a way of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 小型的代表物或供模仿的范例。它可追溯到拉丁语 modellus，即 modus 的指小形式，所以它是“一个小小的尺度”，而不是行事方式。

entries.definition: relating to mode, especially in grammar, music, or logic. It is the adjective; mode is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 与 mode 有关的，尤用于语法、音乐或逻辑。它是形容词，mode 是名词。

entries.definition: fashionable, often with a hint of contempt. It is built from mode in its 'fashion' sense plus -ish.
entries.definitionCN: 时髦的，常带一丝轻蔑。它由表示“时尚”的 mode 加 -ish 构成。

entries.definition: a planned and organized procedure for doing something, often teachable step by step. A mode is the shape of the doing; a method is the route with steps.
entries.definitionCN: 为做某事而计划的、有组织的程序，通常可以一步步传授。mode 是做法呈现的形态，method 是带步骤的路线。

entries.definition: the way in which something is done, often with attention to style or bearing. It is close to mode but more personal and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的方式，常带有风格或举止的意味。它接近 mode，但更个人化，技术性更弱。

entries.definition: the most general word for how something is done. It can replace mode in most everyday sentences, though not in fixed terms such as mode of production.
entries.definitionCN: 表示“如何做”的最通用词。它在多数日常句子里可以替换 mode，但不能替换 mode of production 这类固定说法。

entries.definition: a prevailing custom or style, and also 'in the manner of'. It overlaps with mode in the sense 'current style', but mode is far more formal there.
entries.definitionCN: 流行风俗或款式，也可表示“以……的方式”。它在“当下款式”一义上与 mode 重叠，但 mode 在该义上正式得多。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin modus 'measure', the PIE root *med-, and the English family modal, modality, model, and modify.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 modus“尺度”、原始印欧语词根 *med-，以及英语词族 modal、modality、model、modify。

normal.en: modus is Latin for 'measure'. A mode is the measure an action is cut to, which is why the word covers ways, settings, and styles at once.
normal.cn: modus 是拉丁语的“尺度”。mode 就是一个动作被裁成的尺寸，所以这个词同时覆盖方式、设置与款式。

normal.en: The fixed phrases keep the measure visible: mode of transport, mode of production, mode of operation.
normal.cn: 固定短语把“尺度”保留在明面上：交通方式、生产方式、运作方式。

normal.en: mood 'state of mind' is not related: it comes from Old English mod. Only grammatical mood is a variant of mode.
normal.cn: mood“心境”与它无关：它来自古英语 mod。只有语法上的 mood 才是 mode 的变体。

normal.en: model is a 'little measure' (Latin modellus), a pattern to copy, not a way of doing.
normal.cn: model 是“小小的尺度”（拉丁语 modellus），指供模仿的范本，而不是行事方式。

normal.en: modal, modality, and multimodal all keep the noun's stem; they describe the form or the channel, not the fashion.
normal.cn: modal、modality、multimodal 都保留了这个名词的词干；它们描述形式或通道，而不指时尚。

abstract.en: Picture a tailor's ruler laid on cloth. The ruler does not decide what the cloth is for; it only fixes the shape. Mode is that ruler applied to an action.
abstract.cn: 想象一把裁缝尺压在布上。尺子不决定布用来做什么，只固定形状。mode 就是那把量在动作上的尺子。

abstract.en: A switch with several positions is a row of modes: each position is a stable measure the machine can return to.
abstract.cn: 一个有多个挡位的开关就是一排模式：每个挡位都是机器可以回到的稳定尺度。

abstract.en: Fashion is a measure everyone agrees to wear for a season; that is why the same word can mean 'way' and 'style'.
abstract.cn: 时尚就是大家在一季里共同同意穿着的尺度；正因如此，同一个词既能指“方式”，又能指“款式”。

examples.en: The city's buses and trains are two modes of the same public transport system.
examples.cn: 城市的公交与地铁是同一套公共交通系统里的两种方式。

examples.en: Please leave the phone in silent mode during the examination.
examples.cn: 考试期间请把手机留在静音模式。

examples.en: The historian argues that a new mode of production changed the family as well as the factory.
examples.cn: 这位历史学家主张，新的生产方式不仅改变了工厂，也改变了家庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: “摸的”——先摸清门道，量好尺寸再动手，什么东西就按什么方式做 → mode 方式、模式（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 modus“尺度、方式”，核心是“按一把量好的尺子去做，形成固定的做法”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of mode, all cut from one measure: a ruler that fixes the shape of an action, a machine setting, a melody, a verb form, or a whole way of life.
sensesIntro.cn: mode 的九个义项都从同一把尺子上裁下：它固定一个动作、一个设备设置、一段旋律、一种动词形式或一整种生活形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler laid on something to fix its shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子压在事物上，固定它的形状。

branches.en: MEASURE APPLIED: a human action takes a shape, and a machine takes a repeatable setting.
branches.cn: 尺度落下：人的动作被定形，机器被调到一个可重复的设置。

branches.en: ORGANIZED MEANS: transport and production each settle into a measured arrangement of vehicles, tools, and labour.
branches.cn: 有组织的手段：运输与生产各自固定成由车辆、工具与劳动组成的被量定安排。

branches.en: STYLE AND SONG: the measure becomes the fashion of a season and the interval pattern of a melody.
branches.cn: 款式与歌曲：这把尺子变成一季的时尚，也变成旋律的音程模式。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the verb's form is the measure of the speaker's attitude.
branches.cn: 语法：动词的形式成为说话人态度的尺度。

branches.en: DATA AND LIFE: the mode is where data pile up, and a mode of life is the whole pattern a person is cut to.
branches.cn: 数据与生活：众数是数据堆积之处，而生活方式是一个人被裁成的整体格局。

intro.en: Mode is a Latin noun, and mod- is one of the most productive stems in English: -al, -ality, -ish, -ern, -el, -ule, -ify and multi- all attach to it.
intro.cn: mode 是拉丁语名词，mod- 是英语里最能产出的词干之一：-al、-ality、-ish、-ern、-el、-ule、-ify 与 multi- 都能接在它上面。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is modus 'measure', with diminutives modulus and modellus and the verb moderari 'keep within measure'. All of them keep the idea of a fixed proportion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基是 modus“尺度”，另有指小形式 modulus 与 modellus，以及动词 moderari“保持在尺度之内”。它们都保留“固定比例”的意思。

items.meaningCN: 方式；模式（拉丁语“尺度、方式”）
items.example: The app has a simple mode for beginners.
items.exampleCN: 这个应用为初学者设有一个简单模式。

items.meaning: relating to mode, mood, or form
items.meaningCN: 模态的；语气的（mod- 尺度 + -al 形容词后缀）
items.example: The grammar lesson covers modal verbs such as 'can' and 'must'.
items.exampleCN: 这堂语法课讲 can、must 这类情态动词。

items.meaning: a mode or channel of something
items.meaningCN: 模态；形式；感觉通道（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The study compares visual and auditory modalities.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究比较视觉与听觉通道。

items.meaningCN: 多模态的（multi- 多 + modal 模态的）
items.example: The course uses a multimodal approach with text, sound, and images.
items.exampleCN: 这门课采用文字、声音与图像的多模态方法。

items.meaningCN: 时髦的（mode 时尚 + -ish 形容词后缀）
items.example: The room was furnished in a modish style that dated quickly.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间按一种很快过时的时髦风格布置。

items.meaning: no longer in fashion or use
items.meaningCN: 过时的（out- 超出 + mode 款式 + -ed）
items.example: The factory still runs on outmoded equipment.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂仍在用过时的设备运转。

items.meaningCN: 模型；范本（mod- 尺度 + -el 指小后缀）
items.example: They built a scale model of the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 他们制作了这座桥的比例模型。

items.meaningCN: 现代的（-ern 构成形容词）
items.example: Modern offices rarely keep paper files.
items.exampleCN: 现代办公室很少保存纸质档案。

items.meaningCN: 适度的；使缓和（保持在应有尺度内）
items.example: The region has a moderate climate.

items.meaning: to change in measure or detail
items.example: The engineers modified the valve to reduce flow.
items.exampleCN: 工程师改动了阀门以减少流量。

items.meaningCN: 模块；单元（mod- 尺度 + -ule 指小后缀）
items.example: The software is built from reusable modules.
items.exampleCN: 这个软件由可复用的模块构成。

items.meaning: to adjust in measure, tone, or strength
items.meaningCN: 调节；调制（按小尺度调整）
items.example: She modulated her voice so as not to wake the baby.
items.exampleCN: 她压低并调节了声音，以免吵醒婴儿。

senses.title: A small copy of a thing
senses.definition: a representation of an object, usually smaller and often built to scale
senses.definitionCN: 某物的再现，通常更小，且常按比例制作
senses.example: The museum displayed a model of the ship.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出了那艘船的模型。
senses.why: The word began as a measured pattern, and the first thing a pattern produces is a reduced copy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指量出来的样板，而样板造出的第一件东西就是缩小的复制件。

senses.title: A person who poses
senses.titleCN: 摆姿势供人描绘或拍摄的人
senses.definition: a person who poses for artists, photographers or fashion shows
senses.definitionCN: 为画家、摄影师或时装表演摆姿势的人
senses.example: She worked as a model for a clothing catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 她为一份服装目录做模特。
senses.why: A living body can also stand in for an ideal body, so the copy became a person.
senses.whyCN: 活人的身体也能充当理想身体的替身，于是复制件变成了人。

senses.title: An example worth copying
senses.definition: a person or thing whose behaviour is held up for others to imitate
senses.definitionCN: 其行为被举出来供他人模仿的人或事物
senses.example: Older students serve as models for the younger ones.
senses.exampleCN: 高年级学生为低年级学生做榜样。
senses.why: Once a copy is approved, it becomes the pattern that the next copy must follow.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某个复制件被认可，它就变成下一个复制件必须遵循的样板。

senses.title: A version of a product
senses.definition: one of the versions in which a product is made and sold
senses.definitionCN: 产品被制造与出售的若干版本之一
senses.example: The new model has a longer battery life.
senses.exampleCN: 新型号的电池续航更长。
senses.why: Factories issue each version as a pattern to be copied on the line, so the version itself is called a model.
senses.whyCN: 工厂把每个版本当作流水线上要复制的样板发下去，于是版本本身就被称为型号。

senses.title: A simplified scientific picture
senses.definition: a simplified description of a system that keeps its main features and drops the rest
senses.definitionCN: 保留主要特征、舍弃其余细节的系统简化描述
senses.example: The model explains how heat moves through the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型解释了热如何穿过墙壁。
senses.why: Science replaces the whole object with a stand-in small enough to reason about.
senses.whyCN: 科学用一个小到可以推理的替身来取代整个对象。

senses.title: A set of equations
senses.definition: a mathematical representation whose relations can be solved or simulated
senses.definitionCN: 一种关系可被求解或模拟的数学表示
senses.example: A simple model predicts the queue length.
senses.exampleCN: 一个简单模型能预测排队长度。
senses.why: When the copy is made of relations rather than material, it can be calculated.
senses.whyCN: 当复制件的材质从实物换成关系，它就可以被计算。

senses.title: A computer representation
senses.definition: a program and its data built to imitate a system's behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 为模仿系统行为而建立的程序及其数据
senses.example: Engineers ran the model overnight to test the design.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师整夜运行模型来检验设计。
senses.why: The calculating copy finally moved into a machine, where it could be run again and again.
senses.whyCN: 会计算的复制件最终搬进机器，可以在那里一遍遍运行。

senses.title: To shape something
senses.definition: to form a material into a shape, especially by hand
senses.definitionCN: 把材料做成某种形状，尤指用手
senses.example: He modeled the figure in clay.
senses.exampleCN: 他用黏土塑出那个人像。
senses.why: The verb returns to the workshop: the hand making the copy is the oldest action in the word.
senses.whyCN: 动词回到工坊：手做出复制件，是这个词里最古老的动作。

senses.title: To display clothes
senses.definition: to wear clothes for photographs or a show in order to display them
senses.definitionCN: 穿着服装供拍照或走秀以展示它们
senses.example: They model winter coats in the show.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在秀场上展示冬季外套。
senses.why: The posing sense became a verb when the profession turned the body into a display surface.
senses.whyCN: 当这一职业把身体变成展示面，摆姿势这层意思就动词化了。

senses.title: To base something on
senses.definition: to build or design something using another thing as the pattern
senses.definitionCN: 以另一事物为样板来建造或设计
senses.example: The design was modeled on a fishing boat.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计是以一艘渔船为原型做的。
senses.why: The noun's pattern sense became a verb of copying, which is the last step in the chain.
senses.whyCN: 名词的样板义变成表示复制的动词，这是整条链上的最后一步。

intro.en: Model entered English from French modelle, from Italian modello, from a reconstructed Vulgar Latin diminutive of modulus 'small measure'. The Latin base is modus 'measure'.
intro.cn: model 经法语 modelle、意大利语 modello 进入英语，更早是俗拉丁语中 modulus「小量度」的一个重构指小形式；拉丁语基底为 modus「量度」。

items.en: Latin modus meant measure, manner or limit and underlies mode, moderate and modulus.
items.cn: 拉丁 modus 指量度、方式或限度，是 mode、moderate 与 modulus 的基底。

items.en: Modulus, a small measure or standard unit, was used of a mould, a model and a rhythmic unit.
items.cn: modulus 指小量度或标准单位，曾用于模具、模型与节律单位。

items.en: A Vulgar Latin diminutive of modulus is reconstructed behind the Italian and French words; it is a reconstructed form rather than an attested record.
items.cn: 意大利语与法语词背后的俗拉丁语指小形式为重构所得，是重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Italian modello named a small copy or a pattern, and the artist's model of the Renaissance made the word common.
items.cn: 意大利语 modello 指小复制件或样板；文艺复兴时期画家的模特使这个词通行。

items.en: French modelle carried the word into English in the sixteenth century, first as an architect's pattern and a small copy.
items.cn: 法语 modelle 在十六世纪把词带入英语，最初指建筑师的样板与小复制件。

items.en: English extended the copy to a posing person, then to an example, a product version and a scientific schema; the verb followed in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语把这层复制义扩展到摆姿势的人，再扩展到榜样、产品型号与科学图式；动词用法在十七世纪跟上。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like model; the second group names neighbouring ideas in the same field.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「model」相近；第二组是同一领域里意思相邻的其他说法。

entries.definition: A measured unit or separable part, from the same small-measure root.
entries.definitionCN: 量度单位或可拆分部件，同出那个「小量度」词根。

entries.definition: Relating to mode or manner, as in grammar or music; it keeps the abstract side of modus.
entries.definitionCN: 与方式或调式相关，如语法或音乐；它保留 modus 抽象的一面。

entries.definition: To interfere in others' affairs; it looks close but has no connection with measure.
entries.definitionCN: 插手他人的事；形近，但与「量度」无关。

entries.definition: A person who builds models, formed with the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 建造模型的人，由施动后缀构成。

entries.definition: A hollow shape for casting, from Latin modulus but through a different path; it is the tool, not the copy.
entries.definitionCN: 用于浇铸的空腔形状，虽源于拉丁 modulus，但走的是另一条路径；它是工具，不是复制件。

entries.definition: A copy made to match an original closely, often at full size.
entries.definitionCN: 为贴近原物而做的复制件，常为原尺寸。

entries.definition: The first full working version from which later copies are developed.
entries.definitionCN: 第一个可工作的完整版本，后续复制件由它发展而来。

entries.definition: An original pattern or ideal that later things are said to follow.
entries.definitionCN: 后世事物被认为遵循的原初范式或理想。

entries.definition: An imitation that is run or observed rather than held in the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 被运行或观察、而非拿在手里的仿制品。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin measure word, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「量度」词、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin modus means measure, so a model is a thing measured out to stand for another.
normal.cn: 拉丁 modus 意为量度，因此模型就是量出来代替另一物的东西。

normal.en: The family runs model, modeling, modeler, modeled and remodel.
normal.cn: 同族词有 model、modeling、modeler、modeled 与 remodel。

normal.en: Fixed phrases cover the senses: scale model, role model, fashion model, business model.
normal.cn: 固定说法覆盖各义：比例模型、榜样、时装模特、商业模式。

normal.en: The verb phrase model on keeps the old pattern sense alive.
normal.cn: 动词短语 model on 保留着古老的样板义。

normal.en: British English writes modelled and modelling with a doubled l.
normal.cn: 英式英语把过去式与现在分词写成双写 l 的 modelled 与 modelling。

abstract.en: A model is a stand-in you can hold, rotate and point at.
abstract.cn: 模型是一个能拿住、转动并指给人看的替身。

abstract.en: A role model is the same stand-in made of a person's conduct.
abstract.cn: 榜样是用一个人的行为做成的同一个替身。

abstract.en: A computer model is a copy with no weight, run again and again.
abstract.cn: 计算机模型是一个没有重量的复制件，可以一遍遍运行。

examples.en: The engineer built a scale model before the full bridge was ordered.
examples.cn: 工程师在整座桥下单之前做了一个比例模型。

examples.en: Her calm reply became a model for the whole team.
examples.cn: 她沉着的回答成了整个团队的榜样。

examples.en: The lab models the river's flow on a supercomputer.
examples.cn: 实验室在一台超级计算机上模拟这条河的流量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「模」就是模子，「豆」是小粒——照着模子倒出小粒，就是模型

root: 拉丁 modus「量度」→ modulus「小量度」→ 俗拉丁语指小形式（重构形式）→ 意大利 modello／法语 modelle→ 英语 model。与 mode、moderate、module 同根；与 meddle「插手」形近但无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses follow one measured stand-in: a reduced copy, a posing body, an example, a product version, a scientific picture, equations, a computer representation, the act of shaping, the act of displaying, and the act of basing on.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项跟着同一个量出来的替身：缩小的复制件、摆姿势的身体、榜样、产品型号、科学图景、方程、计算机表示、塑造的动作、展示的动作，以及以之为原型的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scaled wooden body on a table, with the same lines drawn on paper beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上放着一具按比例缩小的木制车身，旁边摊着画出同样线条的图纸。

branches.en: THE COPY MADE BY HAND: a reduced object is built, and the hand that builds it is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 亲手做出的复制件：一个缩小的物件被造出来，造它的那只手是最古老的一层。

branches.en: THE POSING BODY: a living person stands in for an ideal body, and the same act becomes a verb.
branches.cn: 摆姿势的身体：活人替理想身体站台，同一个动作又动词化。

branches.en: THE APPROVED PATTERN: a copy that has won approval becomes the thing others must follow.
branches.cn: 被认可的样板：赢得认可的复制件变成他人必须跟随的东西。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT VERSION: a factory issues each version as the pattern to copy on the line.
branches.cn: 产品型号：工厂把每个版本当作流水线上要复制的样板。

branches.en: THE CALCULATED STAND-IN: a picture, a set of equations, a program, or the act of building on a pattern.
branches.cn: 被计算的替身：一幅图景、一组方程、一个程序，或以样板为据来建造的动作。

intro.en: Model is built on the Latin measure word modus, with the Latin diminutive modulus behind it.
intro.cn: model 建立在拉丁语「量度」词 modus 之上，背后还有拉丁指小词 modulus。

latinIntro.en: Latin modus gives modulus; a reconstructed Vulgar Latin diminutive passes through Italian modello and French modelle into English.

definition_en: belonging to the present age; using the newest methods and design; of art that breaks with tradition; and open rather than old-fashioned in outlook

sceneCN: 这里是「现代派的」（第 3 个义项：与二十世纪反传统艺术风格相关）；句意为整座新翼展厅都用来陈列上个世纪的现代派绘画。图中可辨识物件：色块画作、展签、拍照的观众。
