senses.title: Belonging to the present age
senses.definition: of the present time or the recent past, as opposed to ancient times
senses.definitionCN: 属于当下或近期的，与古代相对
senses.example: Modern borders in this region were drawn less than a century ago.
senses.exampleCN: 这一地区的现代边界是不到一百年前划定的。
senses.why: Late Latin modernus was built from modo, just now, so the word first pointed at whatever belongs to the moment rather than at a fixed era.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 由 modo（就在此刻）构成，所以这个词原本指向属于当下那一刻的东西，而不是某个固定的时代。

senses.title: Using the newest methods or design
senses.definition: made with the latest techniques or materials, and therefore up to date
senses.definitionCN: 用最新技术或材料做成，因而跟得上时代
senses.example: The clinic replaced its old files with a modern records system.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把旧档案换成了新式的记录系统。
senses.why: Anything of the present moment can be assumed to use present methods, so modern slid from a label of time to a label of technique.
senses.whyCN: 凡属于当下这一刻的东西，都可假定用了当下的办法，于是 modern 从时间标签滑成了技术标签。

senses.title: Of art that breaks with tradition
senses.definition: belonging to styles of art, music or architecture that deliberately abandon older rules
senses.definitionCN: 属于有意抛弃旧规矩的艺术、音乐或建筑风格
senses.example: The museum's modern wing puzzled visitors who expected marble columns.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的现代派展区让期待大理石柱的观众摸不着头脑。
senses.why: Artists who broke with the academy needed a name for their own work and took the word for the present age, so modern came to mean a deliberate break rather than a date.
senses.whyCN: 反叛学院派的艺术家需要给自家作品一个名号，便借用「当下时代」这个词，于是 modern 指一次有意的断裂，而不只是标一个日期。

senses.title: Open rather than old-fashioned in outlook
senses.definition: willing to accept new ideas about family, work or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 在家事、工作或行为上愿意接受新观念
senses.example: Her modern attitude toward housework surprised her grandparents.
senses.exampleCN: 她对家务的现代态度让祖父母吃惊。
senses.why: If modern means of this moment, a person who keeps up with the moment is called modern in temper, and the word becomes mild praise for being unshackled from old habits.
senses.whyCN: 如果 modern 指「属于此刻」，那么跟上此刻的人就被称为性情 modern；这个词就这样变成了对「不被旧习惯捆住」的一种温和赞许。

intro.en: Modern goes back to Late Latin modernus, formed from modo, just now, plus a suffix of time; it reached English through French and was first used to contrast the present with the ancient world.
intro.cn: modern 可追到晚期拉丁语 modernus，它由 modo（就在此刻）加一个时间后缀构成；经法语进入英语，最初用来把当下与古代世界对照。

items.en: Modo was an adverb meaning just now or only a moment ago, and it supplied the seed of the word for what belongs to the present.
items.cn: modo 是一个副词，意为「就在此刻、刚才」，它为表示「属于当下」的词提供了种子。

items.en: Modernus is usually dated to the fifth century and was built with the time suffix also seen in hodiernus, of today; its coinage is generally thought to set the present against the ancient past.
items.cn: modernus 一般被认为出现于五世纪，用的是与 hodiernus（今天的）相同的时间后缀；一般认为，这个新造词把当下与古代对立起来。

items.en: French used moderne for what belonged to the current age and passed the word to English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语用 moderne 指属于当前时代的东西，并在十六世纪把这个词传入英语。

items.en: English modern first joined the quarrel of the ancients and the moderns, where it meant the writers and scholars of recent times.
items.cn: 英语的 modern 最早出现在「古代人与现代人之争」里，当时指近代的作家与学者。

items.en: Modern English extended the word to technology, to a style of art that rejects old rules, and to people whose views keep pace with the age.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词扩展到技术、反叛旧规矩的艺术风格，以及观念跟得上时代的人。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem and the English derivatives of modern; the near-meaning group gathers words for what belongs to the present moment.
note.cn: 形近组顺着 modern 的拉丁词干与英语派生词展开；近义组收表示「属于当下这一刻」的词。

entries.definition: The condition or quality of being modern.
entries.definitionCN: 处于现代的状态或性质。

entries.definition: To bring something up to present-day standards.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物提升到当今的标准。

entries.definition: A movement in art and letters that broke with older forms.
entries.definitionCN: 在艺术与文学上打破旧形式的运动。

entries.definition: Following and reacting against the modern movement.
entries.definitionCN: 在现当代运动之后并对其作出反应的。

entries.definition: A believer in or maker of modern styles.
entries.definitionCN: 信奉或创作现代风格的人。

entries.definition: Belonging to the same period, or to the present.
entries.definitionCN: 属于同一时期的，或属于当下的。

entries.definition: Happening or existing now.
entries.definitionCN: 现在正在发生或存在的。

entries.definition: Carrying the newest information or design.
entries.definitionCN: 带有最新信息或设计的。

entries.definition: Having happened a short time ago.
entries.definitionCN: 刚刚发生不久的。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a timestamp built on the Latin adverb for just now, and its family keeps dividing into state, action, movement and believer.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是用拉丁语「就在此刻」造的一个人时间戳，它的词族不断分成状态、动作、流派与信奉者。

normal.en: Modo, Latin for just now, is the root of modern, so the word is a timestamp before it is a style.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 modo 意为「就在此刻」，它是 modern 的词根，所以这个词先是一个时间戳，然后才是一种风格。

normal.en: The suffix that made modernus belongs to the same time-naming kind as the one in hodiernus, of today, which is why the word reads as belonging to now.
normal.cn: 造出 modernus 的那个后缀，与 hodiernus（今天的）里的时间后缀同类，所以这个词读起来就是「属于现在」。

normal.en: Add -ity for the condition, -ize for the act of updating, -ism for the movement, -ist for the person, so one stem covers state, action, style and believer.
normal.cn: 加 -ity 表状态，加 -ize 表更新的动作，加 -ism 表流派，加 -ist 表人，一个词干覆盖状态、动作、风格与信奉者。

normal.en: Postmodern adds post- to modern, marking a reaction against the very style that modern had named.
normal.cn: postmodern 在 modern 前加 post-，标出对 modern 曾经命名的那种风格的反动。

normal.en: The ancients and the moderns were a real quarrel in European letters, and English modern kept the flavour of taking sides in that argument.
normal.cn: 「古代人与现代人之争」是欧洲文坛上一场真实的争论，英语的 modern 一直留着在那场争论里选边站的味道。

abstract.en: Picture a glass wall going up beside a stone wall, the new one clean and the old one weathered.
abstract.cn: 想象一道玻璃墙在石墙旁边立起，新的干净利落，旧的风化斑驳。

abstract.en: A word that began as a timestamp turns into a judgement: to call something modern is also to say it has left the old rules behind.
abstract.cn: 一个起初只是时间戳的词变成了判断：说某样东西 modern，也是在说它把旧规矩留在了身后。

abstract.en: Every modern thing will one day need a newer word, which is why the vocabulary keeps adding post- and neo- in front of it.
abstract.cn: 每一件 modern 的东西终有一天会需要更新的词，所以词汇不断在它前面加上 post- 与 neo-。

examples.en: Modern borders in this region were drawn less than a century ago.
examples.cn: 这一地区的现代边界是不到一百年前划定的。

examples.en: The clinic replaced its old files with a modern records system.
examples.cn: 诊所把旧档案换成了新式的记录系统。

examples.en: Her modern attitude toward housework surprised her grandparents.
examples.cn: 她对家务的现代态度让祖父母吃惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩登」——老上海话里的摩登就是时髦，这个词本来就是借来的 modern；记住 modern 是现代的、新式的。

root: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 由 modo（就在此刻）加时间后缀构成，一般认为首见于五世纪；经法语 moderne 进入英语，先指当代的，再指新式、现代派与开明。

sensesIntro.en: The core is belonging to now; the senses divide into a period, a technique, an artistic revolt, and an open outlook.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「属于此刻」；义项由此分出时代、技术、艺术上的反叛，以及开明的观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass and steel front rising beside an old stone wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面玻璃与钢的立面在旧石墙旁立起。

branches.en: a border line drawn a century ago on an old map
branches.cn: 一张旧地图上不到一百年前划出的边界线

branches.en: paper files replaced by screens in a clinic
branches.cn: 诊所里纸质档案被屏幕取代

branches.en: colour bands on canvas where columns once stood
branches.cn: 画布上的色带，取代了曾经的大理石柱

branches.en: grandparents listening to a granddaughter's plan
branches.cn: 祖父母听孙女讲她的安排

branches.en: the same word for a new machine and a new way of painting
branches.cn: 同一个词，既指新机器，也指新的画法

intro.en: A Latin adverb of the present moment, a time suffix and five English forms carry the word from a date to a style and a temper.
intro.cn: 一个表示当下这一刻的拉丁副词、一个时间后缀，加上五个英语形式，把这个词从日期带到了风格与性情。

latinIntro.en: The reliable Latin core is modo plus the time suffix behind modernus, and hodiernus shows the same pattern of naming what belongs to today.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的拉丁语核心是 modo 加上构成 modernus 的时间后缀，hodiernus 则展示了同样一套「给属于今天的东西命名」的模式。

items.meaningCN: 表示属于某段时间的后缀

definition_zh: 片刻；时刻；时机；重要性
definition_en: a very short period of time; a particular point in time; the right point for doing something; formal importance or weight
core_image: 秒针刚跳过去一格，屋里恰好安静下来
scene: 锅里水刚开，母亲转身去接电话，回来时饺子已经全浮了起来。For a moment the kitchen was quiet enough to hear the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 moment 是「片刻、一会儿」（第 1 个义项：很短的一段时间）；句意为有短短一会儿，厨房安静得能听见雨声。画面里能想见：冒热气的锅、浮起的饺子、响起的电话。

collocations.zh: 关键时刻；见真章的一刻

derivatives.zh: 由 moment 加 -ary 构成，义为「瞬间的；短暂的」
由 momentary 加 -ly 构成，义为「片刻地；马上」
由 moment 加 -ous 构成，义为「重大的；影响深远的」
与 moment 同出拉丁语 momentum，义为「动量；势头」

senses.title: A very short period of time
senses.definition: a very short period of time, often shorter than a minute
senses.definitionCN: 很短的一段时间，常指不到一分钟
senses.example: For a moment the kitchen was quiet enough to hear the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 有短短一会儿，厨房安静得能听见雨声。
senses.why: Latin momentum first meant movement, and a moment is the smallest slice of movement you can notice, a tick of time that passes before anything else happens.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 momentum 起初表示「运动」，而 moment 就是你能察觉的最小一段运动：在别的事情发生之前先溜走的那一格时间。

senses.title: A particular point in time
senses.definition: a particular point in time, especially one that is remembered or waited for
senses.definitionCN: 某个特定的时间点，尤指被记住或等待的那一个
senses.example: The moment the lights went out, everyone froze.
senses.exampleCN: 灯灭的那一刻，所有人都僵住了。
senses.why: Once time is cut into ticks, one tick can be singled out and named; the word then stops being a length and becomes a marked position on the clock.
senses.whyCN: 时间一旦被切成格子，其中一格就能被单独挑出来命名；这个词于是不再表示长度，而表示钟面上的一个标记位置。

senses.title: The right point for doing something
senses.definition: the point at which something is best done, or when an important change becomes possible
senses.definitionCN: 最适合做某事的那个点，或重大变化可能发生的那个点
senses.example: The crisis became the moment for the old policy to end.
senses.exampleCN: 这场危机成了旧政策终止的时机。
senses.why: A single tick can carry a decision: when the word names one point, that point can also be the hinge on which later events turn.
senses.whyCN: 一格时间可以承载一个决定：当这个词指某一个点时，那个点也能成为后来事件转动所绕的轴。

senses.title: Importance or weight, in formal use
senses.definition: importance, especially in the phrase of great moment; a formal and rather old use
senses.definitionCN: 重要性，尤用于短语 of great moment；属正式而偏旧的用法
senses.example: The choice before the council was of great moment.
senses.exampleCN: 摆在议会面前的这个选择分量很重。
senses.why: Latin momentum also meant weight and influence, because something that moves carries force; English kept that sense for serious, formal matters.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 momentum 也指重量与影响力，因为运动的东西带着力量；英语把这个义项留给了严肃正式的场合。

intro.en: Moment is a contraction of a Latin word for movement, and its senses still follow the path from a moving body to a tick of time and to weight.
intro.cn: moment 是拉丁语表示「运动」的词缩合而来，它的义项仍沿着从运动之物到一格时间、再到分量的路线走。

items.en: Movere meant to move, and it supplied a large family of words about motion and change.
items.cn: movere 意为移动，派生出一整族与运动、变化有关的词。

items.en: Movimentum named a movement; in everyday speech the v dropped out and the word became momentum.
items.cn: movimentum 表示一次运动；在日常口语里 v 脱落，词形变成 momentum。

items.en: Momentum covered movement, the smallest division of time, and also weight or influence.
items.cn: momentum 兼指运动、最小的时间单位，以及重量或影响力。

items.en: Old French took the time sense as moment, meaning an instant, and passed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语取其中的时间义，写作 moment，意为瞬间，并传入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the short-time sense as the main one, adds the point-in-time and opportunity senses, and leaves importance to formal style.
items.cn: 现代英语以「短暂时间」为主体义项，又发展出时点与时机义，而「重要性」只留在正式文体里。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin movement root and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for instants, turning points and weight.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语「运动」词根及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示瞬间、转折点与分量的词。

entries.definition: Lasting only for an instant.
entries.definitionCN: 只持续一瞬的；短暂的。

entries.definition: For a very short time, or very soon.
entries.definitionCN: 片刻地；马上。

entries.definition: Of great importance, often because it changes a course of events.
entries.definitionCN: 重大的，常指会改变事态走向的。

entries.definition: The force of a moving body, or the push that keeps a process going.
entries.definitionCN: 运动物体的力；推动进程的势头。

entries.definition: An extremely short moment.
entries.definitionCN: 极短的一瞬。

entries.definition: A very short space of time, used loosely.
entries.definitionCN: 宽松说法中的一小会儿；分钟。

entries.definition: A particular point in time, especially one where decisions must be made.
entries.definitionCN: 特定时刻，尤指必须作决定的关头。

entries.definition: The importance or meaning that something carries.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物所具有的重要性或意义。

normalIntro.en: The word is a shrunk Latin movement word, and every sense is a different reading of what that small movement marks: a tick, a point, a hinge, a weight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「运动」一词的缩形，每个义项都是对那一小段运动所标记之物的不同解读：一格、一点、一轴、一份重量。

normal.en: Movere is Latin for to move; drop the v from movimentum and momentum appears.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语的「移动」；把 movimentum 里的 v 去掉，就得到 momentum。

normal.en: The -ment in movement and the -ment of moment come from the same Latin habit of building nouns out of verbs.
normal.cn: movement 的 -ment 与 moment 的 -ment 源自同一个用动词造名词的拉丁习惯。

normal.en: Momentary adds -ary: lasting only a moment.
normal.cn: momentary 加 -ary：只持续一个片刻的。

normal.en: Momentous adds -ous: full of moment, therefore heavy with importance.
normal.cn: momentous 加 -ous：满是分量，因而是重大的。

normal.en: At the moment points to now; in a moment points to just after now.
normal.cn: at the moment 指向现在；in a moment 指向现在之后的一小会儿。

abstract.en: A moment is what a moving world leaves behind when you stop the film for one frame.
abstract.cn: moment 就是你按下暂停键时，这个运动的世界留下的那一帧画面。

abstract.en: Anything that moves carries weight, which is why the same word can mean both an instant and a serious matter.
abstract.cn: 凡是运动的东西都带着分量，所以同一个词既能指一瞬，也能指严肃大事。

abstract.en: A hinge is a small point that decides which way a large door swings.
abstract.cn: 合页是一个小点，却决定一扇大门往哪边开。

examples.en: For a moment the kitchen was quiet enough to hear the rain.
examples.cn: 有短短一会儿，厨房安静得能听见雨声。

examples.en: The moment the lights went out, everyone froze.
examples.cn: 灯灭的那一刻，所有人都僵住了。

examples.en: The choice before the council was of great moment.
examples.cn: 摆在议会面前的这个选择分量很重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「默默」——沉默的一小会儿，就是片刻；moment 就是片刻、时刻。

root: 拉丁语 movere（移动）派生的 movimentum 缩合为 momentum（运动、瞬间、分量），经古法语 moment 进入英语；同族词多与运动、瞬间有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one tick of movement; the senses read that tick as a brief length, a marked point, a hinge for decisions and a measure of weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一格运动；义项把这一格读成一段短时长、一个标出的点、一处决策的轴心，以及一份分量的尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the second hand jumping one small step while the room falls silent.
core.cn: 核心意象：秒针刚跳过去一小格，屋里恰好安静下来。

branches.en: a kettle whistling, then silence for a breath
branches.cn: 水壶响过之后，静下一口气的工夫

branches.en: everyone looking up as the lights fail
branches.cn: 灯灭时所有人一起抬头

branches.en: a door left open at the exact second it matters
branches.cn: 在关键那一秒被推开的门

branches.en: a council raising a hand at the turning point
branches.cn: 转折点上举手的议事会

branches.en: a heavy file placed on a light table
branches.cn: 重文件压在轻桌子上

intro.en: A Latin verb of moving, its contracted noun, a French instant and four English endings turn a step of movement into time and importance.
intro.cn: 一个表示移动的拉丁动词、它缩合而成的名词、一个法语词和四个英语词尾，把一步运动变成了时间与分量。

latinIntro.en: Movere, movimentum and momentum are recorded Latin forms, and momentum is the direct source of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: movere、movimentum 与 momentum 都是有记录的拉丁词形，其中 momentum 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.meaning: a brief time; a point in time
belonging to, of the nature of
result or means of an action
items.meaningCN: 名词后缀：动作的结果或手段

definition_zh: 妈妈；妈咪（儿语，亲昵称呼）
definition_en: a child's word for mother, used as an affectionate term of address
core_image: 孩子张开双臂扑向的那个人：最亲的怀抱
scene: 小女孩摔破了膝盖，哭着满屋子找人。"Mommy, I need a bandage!" she called from the hallway.
sceneCN: 这里 mommy 是「妈妈、妈咪」（第 1 个义项：孩子对母亲的亲昵称呼）；句意是小女孩在走廊里喊「妈妈，我需要创可贴」。

collocations.zh: （职业女性为照顾孩子放缓升迁的）妈妈轨道

derivatives.zh: 由 mommy 的口语化缩短构成，义为「妈妈」，比 mommy 更通用
同源的婴儿发音型称呼，义为「妈妈」，是更古老的儿语形式
标准称呼形式，义为「母亲」， mommy 是其儿语亲昵变体
由 mommy 加 -hood 后缀构成，义为「妈妈身份；为人母的状态」

senses.title: A child's affectionate word for mother
senses.definition: the word a small child uses to call or talk about its mother, showing closeness and affection
senses.definitionCN: 小孩子呼唤或提及母亲时用的词，表示亲近与依恋
senses.example: The toddler reached out her arms and whispered, "Mommy."
senses.exampleCN: 刚学步的小女孩张开双臂，轻声喊「妈妈」。
senses.why: Baby talk favors the easiest syllables ma-ma, so the affectionate reduplicated form became the child's name for the person who holds and feeds them.
senses.whyCN: 儿语偏爱最容易发的叠音 ma-ma，这个重复的亲昵形式自然成为孩子对那个怀抱自己、喂养自己的人的称呼。

senses.title: A mother figure viewed through a child's eyes
senses.definition: a mother regarded from the child's perspective, as the one who comforts, protects and decides
senses.definitionCN: 从孩子视角看的母亲——那个安慰、保护并替自己做决定的人
senses.example: Only mommy can kiss the pain away and make the tears stop.
senses.exampleCN: 只有妈妈能吻走疼痛，让眼泪停下来。
senses.why: Because the word belongs to the child's world, it carries the child's view of the mother: comfort-giver, protector and authority in one small person.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词属于孩子的世界，它天然带着孩子眼中的母亲形象：安慰者、保护者，以及孩子小世界里说了算的人。

intro.en: Mommy belongs to the universal family of nursery syllables built on ma-, the sound babies make earliest and most easily.
intro.cn: mommy 属于以 ma- 为基础的儿语大家族——这是婴儿最早、最容易发出的音。

items.en: The reconstructed nursery form *mma / *ama, a reduplicated labial syllable, is generally believed to be the origin of mother words across many unrelated languages.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构形式 *mma / *ama 是一个重复的唇音音节，是许多互不相关语言中「母亲」一词的共同源头。

items.en: Old English had modor for the adult word, while nursery forms such as mamme were used by children in speech.
items.cn: 古英语的正式称呼是 modor，儿语中则使用 mamme 一类的形式。

items.en: Forms like mame and mamme appear in child-directed speech; mamma and momme variants spread through the nursery vocabulary.
items.cn: mame、mamme 等形式出现在面向幼儿的话语中，mamma、momme 等变体在儿语词汇中流传。

items.en: Mamma became fashionable in polite speech; in America the shortened mom arose, with mommy as its diminutive.
items.cn: mamma 在文雅口语中风行；美国产生了缩短形式 mom，mommy 则是其亲昵小称。

items.en: Mommy established itself as the standard American nursery word for mother, alongside British mummy.
items.cn: mommy 成为美式英语中称呼母亲的标准儿语词，与英式的 mummy 并行。

items.en: Today mommy is the affectionate child's word for mother in American English, also used playfully by adults.
items.cn: 如今 mommy 是美式英语中孩子对母亲的亲昵称呼，成人有时也戏谑使用。

note.en: Do not confuse the nursery word mommy with its formal cousin mother, or with the British spelling mummy, which also names an Egyptian wrapped corpse.
note.cn: 不要把儿语 mommy 与正式的 mother 混淆，也不要与英式拼写 mummy 混淆——后者还指埃及木乃伊。

entries.definition: the British nursery word for mother, identical in origin but spelled differently; also a preserved dead body in ancient Egypt
entries.definitionCN: 英式儿语「妈妈」，与 mommy 同源但拼写不同；另指古埃及木乃伊（同一拼写，另一词源）

entries.definition: an older nursery form for mother, also the anatomical term mamma for a breast or milk gland
entries.definitionCN: 更古老的儿语「妈妈」形式；解剖学中 mamma 又指乳房、乳腺

entries.definition: the everyday American short form of mother, less childish than mommy and usable by adults
entries.definitionCN: 美式英语中 mother 的日常简称，比 mommy 少一些孩子气，成人也常用

entries.definition: the standard word for a female parent, neutral in register where mommy is baby talk
entries.definitionCN: 「母亲」的标准说法，语体中性；mommy 则是儿语

entries.definition: an informal, slightly old-fashioned word for mother, built on the same baby sound ma-
entries.definitionCN: 「妈妈」的非正式说法，略带旧时口吻，同样建立在婴儿音 ma- 上

entries.definition: a clipped colloquial word for mother, common in informal American speech
entries.definitionCN: 「妈」的口语缩略说法，美式非正式口语常用

normalIntro.en: Use the baby sound and the family spellings to fix mommy in memory.
normalIntro.cn: 用婴儿音和同族拼写把 mommy 牢牢记住。

normal.en: mommy = mom + -y; the suffix -y makes any word sound small and affectionate, so mom + y = "dear mom".
normal.cn: mommy = mom + -y；后缀 -y 让词带上「小而亲昵」的口吻，mom 加 y 就是「亲爱的妈妈」。

normal.en: The first syllable ma- is the oldest baby sound in the world: mama → mom → mommy all grow from it.
normal.cn: 首音节 ma- 是世界上最古老的婴儿音：mama → mom → mommy 都由它生长而来。

normal.en: Compare the spelling pair: American mommy versus British mummy — remember "America has an o, Britain has a u".
normal.cn: 对比拼写：美式 mommy 与英式 mummy——记住「美国用 o，英国用 u」。

normal.en: mommy and daddy rhyme in feeling: both end in -y and both are the child's first names for parents.
normal.cn: mommy 与 daddy 韵味相配：都以 -y 结尾，都是孩子对父母最初的称呼。

normal.en: The plural follows the -y → -ies rule like baby → babies: mommy → mommies.
normal.cn: 复数遵循 -y 变 -ies 的规则，与 baby → babies 相同：mommy → mommies。

abstract.en: Picture a toddler tugging a skirt and repeating ma-ma-ma until the word mommy is born.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小孩拽着裙角反复喊 ma-ma-ma，直到 mommy 这个词诞生。

abstract.en: Hear the -y at the end as a warm little smile attached to the word mom.
abstract.cn: 把词尾的 -y 听成贴在 mom 后面的一个温暖的小微笑。

abstract.en: Feel the chain of closeness: mother (formal) → mom (everyday) → mommy (a child's hug in word form).
abstract.cn: 感受亲昵的链条：mother（正式）→ mom（日常）→ mommy（一个孩子式的拥抱变成了词）。

examples.en: "Mommy, will you read me a story?" asked the little boy at bedtime.
examples.cn: 「妈妈，你能给我读个故事吗？」小男孩睡前问。

examples.en: The worried mommy waited outside the classroom on the first day of school.
examples.cn: 开学第一天，忧心的妈妈在教室外等候。

examples.en: Every mother was once somebody's little child calling for mommy.
examples.cn: 每位母亲都曾是某个喊着要妈妈的小小孩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「毛米」——小孩子口齿不清，把「妈咪」喊成「毛米」，毛茸茸的怀抱里是妈妈；mommy 由此记牢。

root: 一般认为源自婴儿最早的唇音叠音节 ma-ma（重构形式 *mma / *ama），属于跨语言的儿语普遍现象；mommy 是 mom 加亲昵后缀 -y 的形式，与古英语 mamme、中世纪英语 mamme 同族，并非拉丁词根，故无拉丁同源词。

sensesIntro.en: From the baby sound ma-ma, mommy first names the mother a child calls for, then extends to the mother figure as the child sees her.
sensesIntro.cn: 从婴儿音 ma-ma 出发，mommy 先指孩子呼唤的母亲，再引申为孩子眼中的母亲角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child's arms reaching for the one person who is comfort and safety
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子张开双臂扑向的那个既是安慰又是安全的人

branches.en: The nursery sound becomes the child's word for mother
branches.cn: 儿语音成为孩子对母亲的称呼

branches.en: Calling the name is calling for comfort and help
branches.cn: 喊出称呼就是在呼唤安慰与帮助

branches.en: The mother figure stands as protector in the child's small world
branches.cn: 母亲角色在孩子的小世界里充当保护者

branches.en: Authority and decisions also belong to this figure
branches.cn: 这一角色也是孩子世界里做主的人

branches.en: The -y ending wraps the whole bond in affection
branches.cn: 后缀 -y 给整层亲情裹上亲昵的外衣

intro.en: Mommy is not built from Latin roots; its parts are the baby syllable ma- and the English affectionate suffix -y.
intro.cn: mommy 并非由拉丁词根构成；它的组成是婴儿音节 ma- 和英语亲昵后缀 -y。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no cognate here: the word belongs to nursery language, so the Latin-related slot stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在此无同源词：这个词属于儿语范畴，拉丁相关条目留空。

items.meaning: the earliest baby sound, base of mother words worldwide
items.meaningCN: 最早的婴儿音，全世界「母亲」一词的基础
items.example: mama is almost the same in hundreds of unrelated languages
items.exampleCN: mama 在数百种互不相关的语言中几乎一模一样

items.meaning: makes a word small, familiar, affectionate
items.meaningCN: 使词带上「小、熟稔、亲昵」的口吻
items.exampleCN: dog 变 doggy，mom 加 y 变 mommy

items.meaning: another affectionate ending in family words
items.meaningCN: 家庭称呼里另一个亲昵词尾
items.exampleCN: aunt 变 auntie，再加 granny 一词

items.example: mommyhood describes life as a mommy
items.exampleCN: mommyhood 描述为人母的生活

items.meaning: the formal base word for a female parent
regional short forms of mother (British mum, American mom)
items.meaningCN: mother 的地域简称（英式 mum、美式 mom）
items.example: mum is the British everyday word

items.meaning: British spelling of mommy; separately, an embalmed body
items.meaningCN: mommy 的英式拼写；另有「木乃伊」义（不同词源）
items.example: British children say mummy, American children say mommy
items.exampleCN: 英国孩子说 mummy，美国孩子说 mommy

items.meaning: a career path slowed down for child care
items.meaningCN: 为照顾孩子而放缓的职业路径
items.example: she chose the mommy track for two years
items.exampleCN: 她选择了两年的妈妈轨道

mommy 的口语缩短形式，义为「妈妈」
同族儿语形式，义为「妈妈」

definition_zh: 钱；货币；财富；款项
definition_en: coins and notes used to buy things; wealth in general; funds collected or set aside for a purpose; the pay received for work
core_image: 铁盒里一叠皱巴巴的纸币，被手指一张张抹平
scene: 集市快收摊了，父亲把皱巴巴的纸币一张张抹平，再塞进旧铁盒。He counted the money twice before putting it in the tin.
sceneCN: 这里 money 是「钱、货币」（第 1 个义项：用来买东西的钱币）；句意为他把钱数了两遍，才放进铁盒。画面里能想见：收摊的集市、皱巴巴的纸币、旧铁盒。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 monet- 加 -ary 构成，义为「货币的；金融的」
由 monet- 加 -ize 构成，义为「使货币化；靠……赚钱」
由 money 加 -ed 构成，义为「有钱的」
由 money 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无钱的」

senses.title: Coins and notes used to buy things
senses.definition: the coins and notes that people use to buy and sell things
senses.definitionCN: 人们用来买卖东西的硬币与纸币
senses.example: He counted the money twice before putting it in the tin.
senses.exampleCN: 他把钱数了两遍，才放进铁盒。
senses.why: The Latin word moneta began as the name of the mint where Roman coins were struck, then slid from the place of making to the thing made.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 moneta 起初是罗马铸币厂的名字，后来从「制造的地点」滑到「造出来的东西」。

senses.title: Wealth in general
senses.definition: wealth considered as a whole, including property and savings as well as cash
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体看待的财富，除现金外还包括房产与积蓄
senses.example: The family lost all its money in the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 这场火让这家人失去了全部财产。
senses.why: Once a word means coins, it easily widens to everything those coins can buy, so money comes to stand for the whole pile rather than the pieces.
senses.whyCN: 一个词一旦指硬币，就很容易扩到这些硬币能买下的一切；于是 money 转而指整堆财富，而不是一枚枚硬币。

senses.title: Funds set aside for a purpose
senses.definition: money collected or kept for a particular aim, such as building a school or running a service
senses.definitionCN: 为某个特定目标筹集或留存的钱，如建校或维持服务
senses.example: The council put public money into the new library.
senses.exampleCN: 议会把公共资金投进了新图书馆。
senses.why: Money is countable in this sense as sums set apart: the word no longer asks what you own but what has been assigned to a job.
senses.whyCN: 在这个义项里，money 可以按「分拨出来的款项」计数：它问的不再是你有多少，而是哪一笔钱被派了什么用途。

senses.title: Pay received for work
senses.definition: the amount a person is paid for their work, often judged as good or bad
senses.definitionCN: 一个人工作所得的报酬，常以高低来评价
senses.example: The money is good, but the hours are long.
senses.exampleCN: 报酬不错，可是工时太长。
senses.why: When money is what a job hands over, the same word measures a wage, and the phrase the money is good simply reports that the pay is generous.
senses.whyCN: 当 money 指一份工作交到你手里的东西时，同一个词就在衡量工资；the money is good 这句话只是说明报酬丰厚。

intro.en: Money comes from a Latin name for a mint, which itself grew from a verb meaning to warn; the place of coin-making gave its name to the coins.
intro.cn: money 来自拉丁语中对铸币厂的称呼，而那个称呼又长自动词「警告」；造币之地把自己的名字给了造出来的钱。

items.en: Monere meant to warn or to advise, and it stands behind the epithet of Juno whose temple held the Roman mint.
items.cn: monere 意为警告、提醒，朱诺的称号就由它而来，而罗马铸币厂正设在朱诺神庙里。

items.en: Moneta first named the mint, the place where silver was struck into coin, and later the coin itself.
items.cn: moneta 先指铸币厂，即把白银打成硬币的地方，后来也指硬币本身。

items.en: A monetarius was an officer of the mint, and the adjective monetarius described anything belonging to coining.
items.cn: monetarius 是铸币厂的官吏，而同形的形容词表示「与铸币有关的」。

items.en: Old French moneie carried the coin sense and also the sense of coined wealth into everyday use.
items.cn: 古法语 moneie 把「硬币」义以及「由钱构成的财富」义带入日常使用。

items.en: Modern English money keeps the mass-noun sense, adds funds and pay, and allows the formal plural monies for separate sums.
items.cn: 现代英语的 money 保留不可数名词的用法，又添上「资金」与「报酬」，并允许用正式复数 monies 指分开的多笔款项。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin mint word and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for cash, circulating value and wealth.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语「铸币厂」一词及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示现金、流通价值与财富的词。

entries.definition: Connected with money or the currency of a country.
entries.definitionCN: 与货币或一国通货有关的。

entries.definition: To turn something into a source of money.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物变成赚钱的来源。

entries.definition: Rich, or coming from wealthy people.
entries.definitionCN: 有钱的，或来自富裕阶层的。

entries.definition: The place where a country makes its coins.
entries.definitionCN: 一国制造硬币的地方；铸币厂。

entries.definition: Coins and notes in hand, rather than money in an account.
entries.definitionCN: 手头的硬币和纸币，区别于账户里的钱。

entries.definition: The money a country uses and that is accepted in it.
entries.definitionCN: 一国使用并在该国通行的货币。

entries.definition: A large amount of money and property owned by someone.
entries.definitionCN: 某人拥有的大量钱财与财产。

entries.definition: Money available to be spent for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 可供用于某个目的的钱；资金。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the name of a building where coins were made, and its family keeps returning to mints, currency and the wealth coins stand for.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是一处造币建筑的名字，词族反复回到铸币厂、通货，以及硬币所代表的财富。

normal.en: Moneta is Latin for a mint, so money first names the place where coin is made, then the coin that came out.
normal.cn: moneta 是拉丁语的「铸币厂」，所以 money 先指造币的地方，再指造出来的硬币。

normal.en: Monetary adds -ary to the stem monet-: anything belonging to money.
normal.cn: monetary 在词干 monet- 后加 -ary：属于货币的一切。

normal.en: Monetize adds -ize: to turn a thing into money or into a way of earning.
normal.cn: monetize 加 -ize：把某样东西变成钱或变成赚钱的方式。

normal.en: Moneyed adds -ed: supplied with money, therefore rich.
normal.cn: moneyed 加 -ed：有钱供着，因而是富有的。

normal.en: Money is usually uncountable, so we say much money or a sum of money, not a money.
normal.cn: money 通常不可数，所以说 much money 或 a sum of money，而不说 a money。

abstract.en: A mint is a room where metal is pressed into promises; the word carries that promise long after the building is gone.
abstract.cn: 铸币厂是把金属压成承诺的房间；建筑早已不在，这个词仍带着那份承诺。

abstract.en: The same word covers a coin, a fortune and a budget because all three are the same thing at different scales.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖一枚硬币、一笔家产和一份预算，因为这三者只是同一件东西的不同尺度。

abstract.en: Counting money twice is an old habit: value felt in the hand is heavier than value written in an account.
abstract.cn: 把钱数两遍是老习惯：握在手里的价值，比写在账上的价值更沉。

examples.en: He counted the money twice before putting it in the tin.
examples.cn: 他把钱数了两遍，才放进铁盒。

examples.en: The family lost all its money in the fire.
examples.cn: 这场火让这家人失去了全部财产。

examples.en: The council put public money into the new library.
examples.cn: 议会把公共资金投进了新图书馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马尼」——听着像马驮着的尼龙袋，里面装的全是钱；money 就是钱。

root: 拉丁语 moneta（罗马的铸币厂，设在朱诺神庙）经古法语 moneie 进入英语；同族词多与铸币、货币、财富有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is coin struck at a mint; the senses widen from coin to the whole of one's wealth, to funds tied to a purpose, and to the pay a job brings.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是在铸币厂打出的硬币；义项从硬币扩到全部家产、指定用途的资金，以及工作带来的报酬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of crumpled notes being smoothed flat and tucked into a tin box.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠皱巴巴的纸币被抹平，塞进铁盒。

branches.en: a handful of coins pushed across a counter
branches.cn: 几枚硬币被推过柜台

branches.en: a tin box holding the savings of a whole family
branches.cn: 一只装着一家人积蓄的铁盒

branches.en: a house and a field counted as one estate
branches.cn: 把房子和田地算作同一份家产

branches.en: a labelled jar of funds for a new roof
branches.cn: 贴着标签、攒着修屋顶的资金罐

branches.en: a pay slip read twice at the kitchen table
branches.cn: 在厨房桌上看了两遍的工资单

intro.en: A Latin verb of warning, the mint it named, the officer of that mint and four English endings carry the word from a building to cash, wealth and pay.
intro.cn: 一个表示「警告」的拉丁动词、它命名的铸币厂、厂里的官吏，以及四个英语词尾，把这个词从一座建筑带到了现金、财富与报酬。

latinIntro.en: Monere, moneta and monetarius are recorded Latin forms; the mint word is the direct ancestor of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: monere、moneta 与 monetarius 都是有记录的拉丁词形，其中表示铸币厂的那个词是英语名词的直接祖先。

definition_zh: 显示器；监测仪；班长；监督者；监测；监控；监听
definition_en: a device that displays or records information, a person who warns or keeps order, or to watch and check something continuously over time
core_image: 一个站在旁边不断提醒“注意”的人，眼睛一直盯着同一处
scene: 控制室里，工程师盯着显示管道压力的监视器。From the control room the engineer watched the monitor that showed the pressure inside the pipeline.
sceneCN: 这里 monitor 是「显示器」（第 1 个义项：显示画面或数据的屏幕）；句意：工程师在控制室里盯着显示管道内压力的显示器。场景要点：昏暗的控制室、一排亮着的屏幕、屏幕上跳动的压力曲线、管道剖面图；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A screen that shows the picture
senses.definition: a screen, especially a computer or television display, that shows information or a picture
senses.definitionCN: 显示信息或画面的屏幕，尤指电脑或电视显示屏
senses.example: The second monitor shows the camera feed from the front door.
senses.exampleCN: 第二块显示器显示前门的摄像头画面。
senses.why: Broadcasting used a monitor for a device that continuously checked a transmission, and the screen showing that check took the name. A computer display repeats the role: it lets someone keep watch on what the machine is doing.
senses.whyCN: 广播业曾把持续检查传输质量的设备称为 monitor，显示这项检查的屏幕便沿用了这个名字。电脑显示器重复着同一角色：让人持续看清机器在做什么。

senses.title: An instrument that keeps watch
senses.definition: a device that continuously measures and displays a physical condition, such as heart rate or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 持续测量并显示某项身体或物理状况的设备，如心率或压力
senses.example: The heart monitor began to beep faster and faster.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏监测仪开始越响越快地鸣叫。
senses.why: The Latin monitor was a person who warned. An instrument that watches a pulse and sounds an alarm takes over the warning job, so the person's title passes to the machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monitor 是一个发出警告的人。一台盯着脉搏、并发出警报的仪器接过了这份警告的职责，于是人的称呼转移到了机器上。

senses.title: The pupil who keeps order
senses.definition: a senior pupil at a school given the task of keeping order or checking attendance
senses.definitionCN: 学校里被赋予维持秩序或检查出勤任务的高年级学生
senses.example: The hall monitor checked the corridors every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 走廊值日生每小时巡查一次走廊。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense, from 1540s: a senior pupil 'charged with keeping order'. The student does exactly what the Latin word says — reminds others of the rules and reports breaches.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最古老的义项，始于 16 世纪 40 年代：受命维持秩序的高年级学生。这个学生做的正是拉丁词所说的——提醒别人守规矩，并报告违规。

senses.title: An official who warns
senses.definition: a person appointed to observe, advise, and warn, especially in an official or technical role
senses.definitionCN: 受指派观察、建议并提出告诫的人，尤指担任正式或技术职务者
senses.example: A monitor was appointed to warn the committee about conflicts of interest.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会任命了一名监督员，就利益冲突提出告诫。
senses.why: Latin monitor meant 'one who reminds, admonishes, or checks', and also 'an overseer, instructor, guide'. The English noun keeps that advisory, warning figure before it ever names a machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monitor 意为“提醒者、告诫者、检查者”，也指“监督者、指导者、引路人”。英语名词先保留了这个提出建议与警告的人，之后才用它命名机器。

senses.title: Watch the numbers over time
senses.definition: to measure and check a quantity or condition regularly over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内定期测量并检查某个数量或状况
senses.example: Sensors monitor the temperature of the tank every ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器每十分钟监测一次储罐的温度。
senses.why: The verb appeared in 1924 for checking the quality of radio signals. Its core is repetition: a monitor does not look once but keeps looking, so the verb means sustained checking rather than a single glance.
senses.whyCN: 动词于 1924 年出现，指检查无线电信号的质量。它的核心是重复：monitor 不是看一眼，而是持续地看，所以这个动词表示持续的检查，而不是一瞥。

senses.title: Keep someone under surveillance
senses.definition: to watch a person, group, or activity closely, especially to detect wrongdoing or risk
senses.definitionCN: 密切注视某人、某群体或某项活动，尤为了发现不当行为或风险
senses.example: The company monitors its drivers' speed and braking through an app.
senses.exampleCN: 公司通过一个应用监控司机的车速与刹车情况。
senses.why: When the watching is turned from a gauge to people, the warning role becomes surveillance. The same continuous attention is now aimed at behaviour that may need correcting.
senses.whyCN: 当注视的对象从仪表转向人，提醒的职责就变成了监控。同样的持续关注，现在对准了可能需要纠正的行为。

senses.title: Listen to a channel
senses.definition: to listen to a radio, telephone, or other channel continuously in order to catch particular information
senses.definitionCN: 持续收听无线电、电话或其他频道，以捕捉特定信息
senses.example: They monitored the radio channel all night, waiting for a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整夜监听那个无线电频道，等待回复。
senses.why: The earliest verb sense was exactly this: checking radio signals for quality. Listening to a channel is watching with the ears, and the word's continuity remains.
senses.whyCN: 最早的动词义正是这个：检查无线电信号的质量。用耳朵听一个频道就是“用耳朵看”，而这个词的持续性仍然保留。

senses.title: The lizard that warns
senses.definition: a large lizard of the family Varanidae, called a monitor because of an old story that it warned people of crocodiles
senses.definitionCN: 巨蜥科的大型蜥蜴，因古老传说称它会向人预警鳄鱼而得名
senses.example: A monitor lizard crossed the trail and disappeared into the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 一只巨蜥穿过小径，消失在草丛里。
senses.why: The name was given in 1826 because the lizard was fabled to give warning of Nile crocodiles. It is the same 'warner' sense, applied to an animal rather than a person or device.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字始于 1826 年，因为传说这种蜥蜴会预警尼罗河鳄鱼。它仍是“警告者”这层意思，只是用在了动物身上，而不是人或设备。

senses.title: The ironclad that admonished
senses.definition: the name of the first ironclad warship of that design, built in 1862 and intended as a warning to the Confederacy
senses.definitionCN: 1862 年建造的第一艘该型铁甲舰的名称，意在向南方邦联发出警告
senses.example: The Monitor fought the Merrimack in 1862 and changed naval warfare.
senses.exampleCN: 1862 年，莫尼特号与梅里马克号交战，改变了海战方式。
senses.why: The inventor chose the name because the ship was meant to 'admonish' Confederate leaders. The Latin warner becomes a floating threat, a warning made of iron.
senses.whyCN: 发明者选择这个名字，是因为这艘船意在“告诫”南方邦联的领导人。拉丁语的告诫者变成了浮在水上的威胁，一个用铁铸成的警告。

senses.title: A background watcher in software
senses.titleCN: 软件中的后台监控程序
senses.definition: in computing, a program or process that runs in the background and checks system activity
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，指在后台运行、检查系统活动的程序或进程
senses.example: A background monitor logs every login and flags unusual hours.
senses.exampleCN: 一个后台监控程序记录每次登录，并标记异常时段。
senses.why: Software repeats the human watchman: it runs unnoticed, checks continuously, and reports what looks wrong. The old 'one who warns' is now a loop of code.
senses.whyCN: 软件重复着人类更夫的角色：它不声不响地运行，持续检查，并报告看起来不对的地方。古老的“告诫者”如今成了一段循环的代码。

intro.en: Monitor began as a Latin word for a person who warns, entered English in the sixteenth century as a school officer, and only in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries became a machine, a lizard, a warship, and finally a screen. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monitor 最初是拉丁语中表示“告诫者”的词，16 世纪作为学校职务进入英语，直到 19 与 20 世纪才变成仪器、蜥蜴、军舰，最后成为屏幕。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'senior pupil at a school charged with keeping order'. It came from Latin monitor.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“受命维持秩序的学校高年级学生”。它来自拉丁语 monitor。

items.en: Latin monitor meant 'one who reminds, admonishes, or checks', and also 'an overseer, instructor, guide, teacher'. It was an agent noun from monere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 monitor 意为“提醒者、告诫者、检查者”，也指“监督者、指导者、引路人、教师”。它是 monere 的施动名词。

items.en: Monere meant 'to remind, bring to one's recollection, tell of; admonish, advise, warn, instruct, teach'. It goes back to PIE *moneie-, a causative form of *men- 'to think', the root also behind Latin memini 'I remember' and mens 'mind'.
items.cn: monere 意为“提醒、使想起、告知；告诫、建议、警告、指导、教导”。它可追溯到原始印欧语 *moneie-，即 *men-“思考”的使役形式；同一词根也是拉丁语 memini“我记得”与 mens“心智”的来源。

items.en: The monitor lizard was so called because it was fabled to warn people of Nile crocodiles (1826). The ironclad warship Monitor (1862) was named by its inventor because it was meant to 'admonish' Confederate leaders.
items.cn: 巨蜥被称为 monitor，是因为传说它会向人预警尼罗河鳄鱼（1826）。铁甲舰莫尼特号（1862）由发明者命名，因为这艘船意在“告诫”南方邦联的领导人。

items.en: The verb is recorded in 1924 meaning 'to check for quality', originally of radio signals. The general sense 'observe, keep under review' is from 1944. Keats had used it in 1818 to mean 'to guide'.
items.cn: 动词于 1924 年有记录，意为“检查质量”，最初用于无线电信号。泛指“观察、持续审视”的义项始于 1944 年。济慈在 1818 年曾用它表示“引导”。

items.en: A broadcasting sense, 'a device to continuously check on the technical quality of a transmission', is recorded from 1931 and led to the sense 'a TV screen displaying the picture from a particular camera'. The computer display is a later extension of that screen sense.
items.cn: 广播义“持续检查传输技术质量的设备”记录于 1931 年，并由此引出“显示某一摄像机画面的电视屏幕”这一义项。电脑显示器是该屏幕义的后期引申。

note.en: The first group separates the noun and adjective forms built on monitor from two related warning words; the second compares the verbs of watching that learners use interchangeably.
note.cn: 第一组把由 monitor 构成的名词与形容词形式，同两个相关的“警告”词分开；第二组比较学习者常互换使用的几个“看管”动词。

entries.definition: the continuous act of checking or watching something. It is the process, while monitor is the device or the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 持续检查或观察的行为。它是过程，而 monitor 是设备或动词。

entries.definition: giving or serving as a warning. It keeps the Latin sense of admonition and is mostly formal.
entries.definitionCN: 给予警告的，或起警告作用的。它保留了拉丁语“告诫”的意思，多用于正式语境。

entries.definition: to warn or reprimand someone firmly but not harshly. It shares the Latin monere root but is a separate verb, not a form of monitor.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定但不严厉地警告或责备某人。它与 monitor 共享拉丁语 monere 词根，但它是另一个动词，不是 monitor 的词形。

entries.definition: a feeling that something is about to happen, especially something bad. It is a warning that comes before the event, built with pre- 'before'.
entries.definitionCN: 一种某事即将发生、尤指坏事的感觉。它是事件之前到来的警告，由 pre-“在前”构成。

entries.definition: to be in charge of people or work and make sure it is done properly. It stresses authority over workers, while monitor stresses continuous checking of signals or conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 负责管理人或工作，确保事情做好。它强调对工作者的权威，而 monitor 强调对信号或状况的持续检查。

entries.definition: to look at something for a period of time, often without measuring it. Monitor usually adds a purpose: to detect change, risk, or poor quality.
entries.definitionCN: 在一段时间内看着某物，通常不进行测量。monitor 通常多一层目的：发现变化、风险或质量问题。

entries.definition: to follow the movement or development of something over time, often by recorded traces. It focuses on where something goes; monitor focuses on whether it stays within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间跟踪某物的移动或发展，常依据记录下来的痕迹。它关注东西去了哪里，monitor 关注它是否仍在限度之内。

entries.definition: to examine people, substances, or signals in order to sort or filter them. It is usually a test applied at a point in time, while monitor is a watch kept over time.
entries.definitionCN: 检查人、物质或信号，以便分类或筛选。它通常是在某一时点施行的检验，而 monitor 是长期保持的观察。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin monere 'warn', the agent noun monitor, and the English family monitoring, monitory, admonish, and premonition.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 monere“警告”、施动名词 monitor，以及英语词族 monitoring、monitory、admonish、premonition。

normal.en: monere means 'to warn, remind'. A monitor is literally 'one who warns' — first a pupil, then an instrument, then a screen.
normal.cn: monere 意为“警告、提醒”。monitor 字面上就是“发出警告的人”——先是学生，再是仪器，最后是屏幕。

normal.en: The school sense is the oldest English one (1540s); the machine and screen senses are centuries later.
normal.cn: 学校职务义是英语里最古老的义项（16 世纪 40 年代）；仪器与屏幕义要晚好几个世纪。

normal.en: The verb arrived in 1924 for checking radio signal quality, which is why 'monitor a channel' still sounds natural.
normal.cn: 动词于 1924 年出现，用于检查无线电信号质量，所以 monitor a channel 至今听起来自然。

normal.en: monitoring is the process, monitory is 'warning', admonish is a separate verb from the same root.
normal.cn: monitoring 是过程，monitory 是“警告的”，admonish 则是同根的另一动词。

normal.en: A monitor differs from a supervisor: it keeps checking a signal or condition, while a supervisor holds authority over people.
normal.cn: monitor 与 supervisor 不同：它持续检查信号或状况，而 supervisor 对人拥有管理权。

abstract.en: Picture a night watchman at a factory gate. He does not repair anything; he looks, checks, and raises the alarm.
abstract.cn: 想象一名守在工厂大门的更夫。他不修理任何东西；他看、检查、发出警报。

abstract.en: Move that watchman into a box on the wall, and he becomes a heart monitor; put his gaze on a screen, and he becomes a display.
abstract.cn: 把这位更夫装进墙上的盒子，他就成了心脏监测仪；把他的目光放到屏幕上，他就成了显示器。

abstract.en: The word always means attention spread over time: a single look is not monitoring, however careful it is.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终表示铺在时间上的注意：只看一眼，无论多仔细，都不算监测。

examples.en: Nurses monitor the patient's pulse and blood pressure every hour.
examples.cn: 护士每小时监测病人的脉搏与血压。

examples.en: The app monitors how much time you spend on each website.
examples.cn: 这个应用监控你在每个网站上花多少时间。

examples.en: The teacher left a monitor in charge of the class while she fetched the keys.
examples.cn: 老师去取钥匙时，让班长负责管班。

dict_mnemonic.text: “莫离他”——莫要离开他，他一直在旁边盯着、随时提醒你 → monitor 监视器；监测（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 monere“警告、提醒”的施动名词 monitor“告诫者”，核心是“持续盯着并随时发出提醒”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of monitor, all held together by one figure: someone standing beside a thing, watching without stopping and speaking up when something is wrong.
sensesIntro.cn: monitor 的十个义项都由同一个形象串起：有人站在某物旁边，不停地看，一有不对就出声提醒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warner standing beside, eyes fixed on one spot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个站在旁边、目光钉在一处的告诫者。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: the warner becomes a measuring device, and the screen that shows its check takes the same name.
branches.cn: 仪器：告诫者变成测量设备，显示这项检查的屏幕也沿用了同一个名字。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the oldest senses keep a person in the role, either a pupil keeping order or an official who warns.
branches.cn: 人：最古老的义项让一个人留在这个角色里，或是维持秩序的学生，或是提出告诫的官员。

branches.en: WATCHING: the verb checks quantities over time, and when aimed at people it becomes surveillance.
branches.cn: 注视：动词随时间检查数量，而当对象转向人时，它就变成监控。

branches.en: LISTENING: a channel is watched with the ears, the earliest verb use of all.
branches.cn: 监听：频道是用耳朵看的，这是所有动词用法中最早的一个。

branches.en: THE NAME TRAVELS: a lizard fabled to warn, an ironclad built to admonish, and a background program that keeps checking.
branches.cn: 名字远行：传说会预警的蜥蜴、为告诫而造的铁甲舰，以及持续检查的后台程序。

intro.en: Monitor is a Latin agent noun in -itor built on mon- 'warn'. English adds -ing, -y, -ial and -ship, while the same root also reaches English through admonish, monition, and premonition.
intro.cn: monitor 是拉丁语中以 -itor 结尾的施动名词，词干 mon- 意为“警告”。英语加上 -ing、-y、-ial 与 -ship，同一词根还通过 admonish、monition、premonition 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is monere 'warn, remind', its agent noun monitor, and the action noun monitio 'a warning'. Summon also belongs here: Latin summonere meant 'hint, remind, warn'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词族包括 monere“警告、提醒”、它的施动名词 monitor，以及行为名词 monitio“警告”。summon 也属于这里：拉丁语 summonere 意为“暗示、提醒、警告”。

items.meaning: one who warns or checks; a checking device
items.meaningCN: 告诫者；检查者；监测设备（mon- 警告 + -itor 施动名词）
items.example: The monitor on the wall showed a steady line.
items.exampleCN: 墙上的监测仪显示出一条平稳的线。

items.meaningCN: 监测；监控（-ing 构成过程名词）
items.example: The patient was kept under close monitoring.
items.exampleCN: 病人被置于密切监测之下。

items.meaningCN: 告诫的；警告的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: He gave a monitory glance at the noisy table.
items.exampleCN: 他朝吵闹的那桌投去一个警告的目光。

items.meaning: relating to a monitor or prefect
items.meaningCN: 级长的；监督的（-ial 构成形容词）
items.example: The monitorial duties rotated each week.

items.meaningCN: 告诫；温和地责备（ad- 向 + mon- 警告）
items.example: The coach admonished the players for arriving late.
items.exampleCN: 教练因球员迟到而告诫了他们。

items.example: She ignored the admonition and drove faster.
items.exampleCN: 她无视那句告诫，反而开得更快。

items.meaning: a warning, especially an official one
items.meaningCN: 警告；正式告诫（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The court issued a monition to the landowner.
items.exampleCN: 法院向那位土地所有者发出正式警告。

items.meaning: a feeling that something is coming
items.meaningCN: 预感；事前警告（pre- 在前 + monition 警告）
items.example: She had a premonition that the flight would be delayed.
items.exampleCN: 她预感到那趟航班会延误。

items.meaningCN: 召唤；传唤（sum- 暗中 + mon- 提醒）
items.example: The manager summoned the clerk to her office.
items.exampleCN: 经理把那名职员叫到办公室。

items.structure: Greek Mentor, perhaps from PIE *men- 'to think'
items.meaningCN: 导师；可信赖的顾问（同出“思考”词根）
items.example: She became a mentor to the younger researchers.
items.exampleCN: 她成了年轻研究者的导师。

latinEntries.meaning: one who warns, reminds, or checks

definition_zh: 月；月份；一个月的时间；漫长的岁月（复数）
definition_en: one of the twelve divisions of the year, also a period of about thirty days and, in the plural, a long stretch of time
core_image: 日历上撕下的一页，边缘还留着月亮的弧度
scene: 月底的夜里，桌上的账单摊开，日期一格一格逼近。The rent falls due at the start of every month.
sceneCN: 这里是「月份、月」（第 1 个义项：日历上的一年十二分之一）；句意为每到月初房租就到期。图中可辨识物件：账单、日历、台灯。

pos.zh: 月；月份；一个月的时间；漫长的岁月

derivatives.zh: 由 month 加 -ly 构成，义为「每月的；每月一次」
由 month 与 long 复合而成，义为「持续一个月的」
由前缀 bi-（两个）加 monthly 构成，义为「两月一次的」

senses.title: One of the twelve divisions of the year
senses.definition: one of the twelve named divisions of the calendar year
senses.definitionCN: 日历年里十二个有名称的划分之一
senses.example: February is the shortest month of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 二月是一年里最短的月份。
senses.why: A month began as the moon's own cycle, so the word for the unit still carries the shape of a turning moon.
senses.whyCN: 月份最初就是月亮自己的一轮周期，所以这个表单位的词里仍留着月亮转动的形状。

senses.title: A period of about thirty days
senses.definition: a span of roughly thirty days used as a unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 用作计时单位的大约三十天的一段时间
senses.example: The repairs took a month to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工作花了一个月才完成。
senses.why: Once the unit is fixed, it can measure any span of about thirty days, whether or not the calendar page matches.
senses.whyCN: 单位一旦固定，它就能用来量任何约三十天的时间段，不必与日历那一页严格对齐。

senses.title: A long stretch of time, in the plural
senses.definition: a long time, used in the plural to suggest a slow wait
senses.definitionCN: 很长的一段时间，用复数来表示漫长的等待
senses.example: She has not written to us for months.
senses.exampleCN: 她好几个月没有给我们写信了。
senses.why: Counting months is slow, so a plural pile of them naturally stands for a long wait.
senses.whyCN: 按月计数本来就慢，于是复数的月份自然就表示一段漫长的等待。

senses.title: The lunar cycle
senses.definition: the period from one new moon to the next, about twenty-nine and a half days
senses.definitionCN: 从一个新月到下一个新月的周期，约二十九天半
senses.example: A lunar month lasts about twenty-nine and a half days.
senses.exampleCN: 一个太阴月约持续二十九天半。
senses.why: The moon-based origin keeps a technical sense alive in astronomy, where a lunar month runs from one new moon to the next.
senses.whyCN: 以月亮为起点的来源让一个术语义在天文学里保留下来：太阴月从一个新月走到下一个新月。

intro.en: The English month is a Germanic word built on the moon, and its oldest sense is a moon-driven cycle rather than a page on a wall.
intro.cn: 英语的 month 是建立在月亮之上的日耳曼词，它最早的意思是被月亮推动的一轮周期，而不是墙上的一页纸。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to measure is generally thought to lie behind the words for moon and month in both the Germanic and the Latin branches.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个表示「测量」的印欧语重构词根同时藏在日耳曼语和拉丁语中表示月亮与月份的词后面。

items.en: Old English mōnaþ joined mōna, the moon, with the noun suffix -þ, so the month was literally the moon's turning.
items.cn: 古英语 mōnaþ 把 mōna（月亮）与名词后缀 -þ 结合，所以月份字面上就是月亮的一轮转动。

items.en: Related forms such as Old Frisian mōnath and German Monat show the same moon-based naming across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 古弗里斯兰语的 mōnath、德语的 Monat 等相关形式显示，日耳曼各语言都用月亮来命名月份。

items.en: Middle English moneth kept the moon inside the word while the spelling slowly moved toward the modern month.
items.cn: 中古英语的 moneth 仍把月亮留在词里，拼写则慢慢向现代形式 month 靠拢。

items.en: Modern English month covers the calendar unit, the lunar cycle and, in the plural, a long stretch of time.
items.cn: 现代英语的 month 兼指日历单位、月相周期，复数还表示很长一段时间。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same moon stem, while the near-meaning group collects the other units used to count time.
note.cn: 形近组收同一月亮词干上的形式，近义组收用来计时的其他单位。

entries.definition: Happening once every month or issued each month.
entries.definitionCN: 由 month 加 -ly 构成，义为「每月的；每月一次」。

entries.definition: The body whose cycle gave the month its name.
entries.definitionCN: 其周期为月份提供名称的天体，月亮。

entries.definition: The day named after the moon, from the same Old English stem.
entries.definitionCN: 以月亮命名的日子，来自同一个古英语词干。

entries.definition: A period of seven days, the unit just below a month.
entries.definitionCN: 七天的一段时间，是比月更小的计时单位。

entries.definition: A period of twelve months.
entries.definitionCN: 十二个月的一段时间。

entries.definition: A period of two weeks, common in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 两周的一段时间，英式用法中常见。

entries.definition: A period of twenty-four hours.
entries.definitionCN: 二十四小时的一段时间。

normalIntro.en: The word is a moon-word from start to finish, and its family keeps returning to cycling light and counted time.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从头到尾都是月亮词，它的同族词也一直回到光的循环与被数出来的时间。

normal.en: Old English mōnaþ is moon plus a noun ending, so the month was named after the moon that paced it.
normal.cn: 古英语 mōnaþ 是月亮加一个名词词尾，月份是用给它定节奏的月亮命名的。

normal.en: German Monat and Dutch maand keep the same m-n shape, which is why the English word looks so plain.
normal.cn: 德语 Monat 与荷兰语 maand 保留同样的 m-n 骨架，所以英语这个词显得格外朴素。

normal.en: monthly adds -ly to month: something that happens once in each month.
normal.cn: monthly 在 month 后加 -ly，表示在每个月发生一次的事物。

normal.en: The plural months often means a long time, as in letters unanswered for months.
normal.cn: 复数的 months 常表示很久，例如好几个月没有回信。

normal.en: Latin mensis is a distant cousin rather than a borrowing, which is why English did not take a Latin shape.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mensis 是远亲而不是借词，所以英语没有采用拉丁语的词形。

abstract.en: A calendar is a row of moons, each one handing its name to a page.
abstract.cn: 日历就是一排月亮，每一个把自己的名字交给一页纸。

abstract.en: Turn a page and a moon has already happened.
abstract.cn: 翻过一页，就有一轮月亮已经走完。

abstract.en: The word is older than paper: people counted months by looking up.
abstract.cn: 这个词比纸更老：人们曾靠抬头看天来数月份。

examples.en: February is the shortest month of the year.
examples.cn: 二月是一年里最短的月份。

examples.en: The repairs took a month to finish.
examples.cn: 修理工作花了一个月才完成。

examples.en: She has not written to us for months.
examples.cn: 她好几个月没有给我们写信了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「忙死」——月底事情多到忙死；记住 month 就是月。

root: 古英语 mōnaþ 由 mōna（月亮）加名词后缀 -þ 构成，本义是月亮的一轮；一般认为它与拉丁语 mensis 同出印欧语表示「测量」的词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the calendar unit, and the senses then branch into a measured span, a slow plural of waiting, and the lunar cycle underneath it all.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是日历上的月份；义项由此分出被丈量的时间段、表示漫长等待的复数，以及藏在底下的月相周期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page torn from a calendar, its edge still curved like a moon.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张从日历上撕下的纸，边缘仍带着月牙的弧度。

branches.en: a calendar page torn off on the first day
branches.cn: 月初撕下的一页日历

branches.en: a repair job stretching across thirty days
branches.cn: 一项横跨三十天的修理活

branches.en: letters left unanswered for a season
branches.cn: 一整个季节无人回的信

branches.en: a chart tracing new moon to new moon
branches.cn: 从新月画到新月的图

branches.en: rent falling due as a month turns
branches.cn: 月份交替时到期的房租

intro.en: The word is held together by a moon noun, an old noun ending, and the two suffixes that turn it into a monthly adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示月亮的名词、一个古老的名词词尾，以及把它变成「每月的」形容词的两个后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin mensis and menstruus belong to the same distant Indo-European family, though English borrowed nothing directly from them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mensis 与 menstruus 属于同一遥远的印欧语族，但英语并没有直接借用它们。

items.meaningCN: 由 moon 与 day 复合

definition_zh: 心情；情绪；气氛；语气（语法）；一时的兴致
definition_en: a temporary state of feeling, or the atmosphere of a place or group, or a grammatical category of the verb
core_image: 天气没有变，屋里的人却觉得整间房子忽明忽暗，像云在屋顶上走
scene: 排练到一半，指挥忽然放下手，说今天先到这里，因为整个乐队已经提不起劲。The conductor stopped the rehearsal because the mood in the hall had gone flat.
sceneCN: 这里 mood 指「一群人当下共同的情绪基调」（第 1 个义项：一时的情绪状态）；句意为指挥中止排练，因为大厅里的情绪已经没了劲。图中可辨识物件：放下的指挥棒、松开的谱架、空着的上半场座位；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 心情；情绪；气氛；语气（语法）
情绪波动；一时的心情变化

derivatives.zh: 情绪化的；闷闷不乐的
闷闷不乐地
喜怒无常
影响情绪的
（设计用的）情绪板

senses.title: A temporary state of feeling
senses.definition: the way a person feels at a particular time, seen as passing rather than fixed
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在某段时间里的感受状态，被视为会过去而非固定
senses.example: The conductor stopped the rehearsal because the mood in the hall had gone flat.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥中止排练，因为大厅里的情绪已经没了劲。
senses.why: the oldest English sense is simply 'mind, disposition', so the word names the weather inside a person rather than their climate.
senses.whyCN: 最早的英语义就是「心境、性情」，因此这个词命名的是人内部的天气，而不是气候。

senses.title: The atmosphere of a place
senses.definition: the feeling that a room, a street or a gathering gives off
senses.definitionCN: 一间屋子、一条街或一场聚会所散发出的感受
senses.example: Candles on the tables changed the mood of the whole restaurant.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上的蜡烛改变了整间餐馆的气氛。
senses.why: the same word moves from one head to a space, because a space is read as having a temper of its own.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从一颗脑袋移到一个空间，因为空间被读作有自己的脾气。

senses.title: A spell of bad temper
senses.definition: a period of sulking or irritability, often named in the plural and with a possessive
senses.definitionCN: 一段闷气或易怒的时期，常以复数并带物主词出现
senses.example: He has been in one of his moods since the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开会之后他一直闹着脾气。
senses.why: when the passing state is unpleasant, the plural turns it into a recurring event that others learn to expect.
senses.whyCN: 当这种会过去的状态并不愉快时，复数把它变成别人学会预期、一再发生的事。

senses.title: A grammatical category
senses.definition: the form of a verb that shows whether it states, commands or supposes
senses.definitionCN: 动词的形式，表明它是在陈述、命令还是假设
senses.example: English marks the imperative mood by leaving the subject out.
senses.exampleCN: 英语通过省去主语来标记祈使语气。
senses.why: this sense is a different word altogether, borrowed from Latin modus 'measure, manner', and it means a manner of speaking.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项其实是另一个词，借自拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」，意思是说话的方式。

senses.title: The public's temper
senses.definition: the general temper of a group, market or electorate at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻一个群体、市场或选民的总体情绪
senses.example: The public mood turned against the plan within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一周之内公众情绪就转向反对这个方案。
senses.why: one person's weather scaled up becomes a collective climate that politicians claim to read.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的天气放大之后成为集体的气候，政治家声称自己能读出它。

senses.title: Feeling like doing something
senses.definition: the inclination to do a particular thing at a particular moment
senses.definitionCN: 在某个时刻做某件具体事情的倾向
senses.example: She was not in the mood for another long explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 她没有兴致再听一段冗长的解释。
senses.why: the state is now aimed at an object, and 'in the mood for' turns a climate into a door that is either open or shut.
senses.whyCN: 这个状态现在有了对象，「有兴致」把气候变成一扇要么开、要么关的门。

senses.title: Rapid shifts of feeling
senses.definition: quick changes between emotional states, often treated as a symptom or a trait
senses.definitionCN: 情绪状态之间的快速变化，常被当作症状或特质
senses.example: Her mood swings made the household walk on glass.
senses.exampleCN: 她的情绪起落让全家人如履薄冰。
senses.why: the plural measures frequency, turning a state into a pattern that others can chart.
senses.whyCN: 复数衡量的是频率，把一个状态变成旁人能画出来的模式。

senses.title: The key of a work
senses.definition: the prevailing feeling that a painting, film or piece of music is built to produce
senses.definitionCN: 一幅画、一部电影或一段音乐被设计来产生的总体感受
senses.example: The grey palette gives the film a mood of waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 灰调子给这部片子一种等待的基调。
senses.why: artists speak of mood because a work also has weather, and the term lets them tune it deliberately.
senses.whyCN: 艺术家谈基调，是因为作品也有天气，而这个说法让他们能刻意调它。

intro.en: English has two different words written mood. The feeling word is native Old English mod 'mind, courage, temper'. The grammar word was borrowed later from Latin modus 'measure, manner', the same source as mode and model. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 英语里有两个写法相同的 mood。表感受的那个是本族古英语 mod「心、勇气、性情」；语法义的那个则是后来从拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」借入的，与 mode、model 同源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mod meant 'mind, inner self, courage, anger'. It is Germanic in origin and had no connection with Latin at all.
items.cn: mod 意为「心、内在自我、勇气、愤怒」。它源出日耳曼语，与拉丁语毫无关联。

items.en: As the older senses faded, the word narrowed to a passing state of feeling, the sense it carries today.
items.cn: 随着较早的义项淡出，这个词收窄为一种会过去的感受状态，也就是今天的义项。

items.en: Modus meant 'measure, standard, manner'. Grammarians used it for the manner in which a verb states or commands, and that use entered English.
items.cn: modus 意为「尺度、标准、方式」。语法学家用它指动词陈述或命令的方式，这一用法进入了英语。

items.en: The spelling fell together in Middle English, so that one shape now carries two unrelated histories, one Germanic and one Latin.
items.cn: 两个词在中古英语里拼写合流，于是一个字形现在背着两段互不相关的历史，一段日耳曼，一段拉丁。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the feeling word was extended to rooms, crowds, markets and works of art, and mood music followed in the twentieth.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，表感受的那个词被延伸到屋子、人群、市场与艺术品，20 世纪又有了「氛围音乐」。

items.en: Source uncertain: the earliest written forms of the Germanic word are attested but its deeper pre-Germanic origin is a reconstruction, and no first date is agreed for the grammar borrowing.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个日耳曼词的最早书写形式有书证，但它在日耳曼语之前的更深来源属重构形式；语法义借入的确切年代也没有公认结论。

note.en: Group one holds the word that looks the same but has another history; group two holds feeling words that differ in duration and cause.
note.cn: 第一组是字形相同而历史不同的词；第二组是持续时间与起因不同的感受词。

entries.definition: From Latin modus 'measure, manner': a way of doing something. It looks close to mood but shares history only with the grammar sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」：做事的方式。字形近 mood，但只与语法义共享历史。

entries.definition: Built on the feeling sense: given to sudden low or irritable states.
entries.definitionCN: 由表感受的义项构成：容易陷入突然的低落或烦躁。

entries.definition: Also from modus through a small form meaning 'little measure'; it belongs to design, not to feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 同样出自 modus，经由一个意为「小尺度」的形式；属设计领域，与感受无关。

entries.definition: From the same idea of measure: kept within limits. Nothing of it survives in the feeling word.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「尺度」这一观念：保持在限度之内。表感受的那个词里没有留下它的痕迹。

entries.definition: A distinct surge such as fear or joy; a mood is the longer weather that such surges happen inside.
entries.definitionCN: 如恐惧或喜悦那样一次明确的涌动；mood 是这些涌动所发生的更长的天气。

entries.definition: A settled tendency to become angry, closer to temperament than to a passing state.
entries.definitionCN: 易怒的固定倾向，更接近气质而非一时的状态。

entries.definition: The feel of a space or occasion; it covers the place sense but never the inner state of one person.
entries.definitionCN: 指空间或场合的感受；覆盖「地点」义，却从不指单个人的内在状态。

entries.definition: A plural word for how high or low someone's cheer is, as in high spirits; it measures level, not colour.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个人兴致高低的复数说法，如兴致高；衡量的是水位，而不是颜色。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The feeling sense is native Old English, while the grammar sense came from Latin modus, so one spelling hides two families.
normal.cn: 感受义是本族古英语，语法义则来自拉丁 modus，因此一个拼写藏着两个词族。

normal.en: The family runs mood, moody, moodily, moodiness, mood-altering, mood board.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mood、moody、moodily、moodiness、mood-altering、mood board。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: in a good mood, in the mood for, mood swings, set the mood.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：心情好、有兴致、情绪波动、定下气氛。

normal.en: Grammar keeps the Latin side alive in phrases like the imperative mood.
normal.cn: 语法在「祈使语气」一类说法里让拉丁那一面活着。

normal.en: Markets and newspapers speak of the public mood, extending one person's weather to a whole country.
normal.cn: 市场与报纸谈「公众情绪」，把一个人的天气扩到整个国家。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the lamp does not change but the walls seem to brighten and dim.
abstract.cn: 想象灯没有变，墙面却似乎忽明忽暗的屋子。

abstract.en: Picture a thermostat that responds to conversation rather than to air.
abstract.cn: 想象一个对谈话而不是对空气作出反应的恒温器。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens only when the person inside feels like it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇只有在里面的人有兴致时才开的门。

examples.en: The mood in the office lifted as soon as the results arrived.
examples.cn: 结果一到，办公室里的气氛就轻松起来。

examples.en: I am not in the mood for a debate tonight.
examples.cn: 我今晚没兴致辩论。

examples.en: The subjunctive mood is rare in modern spoken English.
examples.cn: 虚拟语气在现代英语口语中很少见。

dict_mnemonic.text: mood 读如「木的」——人一时像木头一样闷着 → 心情、情绪、气氛

root: 两条独立来源：表感受的义项出自古英语 mod「心、勇气、性情」，属日耳曼语；表语气的语法义借自拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」，与 mode、model 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a person has weather, and that weather is then read as a room's temper, as a recurring bad spell, as a manner of speaking, as a public climate, as an open door, as a pattern of swings and finally as a key chosen by an artist.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：人有天气，这天气依次被读作一间屋子的脾气、一再出现的坏脾气、一种说话方式、公众气候、一扇开着的门、一串起落的模式，最后是艺术家选定的调子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room whose lamp never changes, yet the walls seem to brighten and dim as clouds cross the roof.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯始终没变的屋子，云从屋顶走过时墙面却忽明忽暗。

branches.en: WEATHER AND ITS RECORD: one sense is a single stretch of feeling, the other the chart of how often it turns.
branches.cn: 天气与它的记录：一个是单段感受，另一个是它翻转频率的图表。

branches.en: A SPACE WITH A TEMPER: the same weather either fills a room or is deliberately composed into a work.
branches.cn: 有脾气的空间：同一种天气要么充满一间屋子，要么被刻意编进一件作品。

branches.en: THE SPELL OTHERS LEARN: a bad mood made plural becomes a recurring event in a household.
branches.cn: 旁人学会的那阵子：坏心情一旦用复数，就成了一户人家反复发生的事。

branches.en: THE OTHER HISTORY: here the word does not mean feeling at all, but the manner in which a verb speaks.
branches.cn: 另一段历史：这里这个词完全不指感受，而指动词说话的方式。

branches.en: CLIMATE AND INCLINATION: one is a whole public's weather, the other a single door that is open or shut.
branches.cn: 气候与意愿：一个是整个公众的天气，另一个是单扇开或关的门。

intro.en: The word is short and native, so the interesting structure lies in its family and in the separate Latin homograph.
intro.cn: 这个词又短又是本族语，因此有意思的结构在它的词族，以及那个同形异源的拉丁词上。

latinIntro.en: Only the grammar sense has Latin behind it, from modus 'measure, manner'; the feeling word has no Latin ancestry at all.
latinIntro.cn: 只有语法义背后有拉丁语，出自 modus「尺度、方式」；表感受的那个词完全没有拉丁来历。

items.example: The mood in the hall went flat.
It forms the adjective for someone given to moods.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容某人容易闹情绪的形容词。

items.meaning: given to low or irritable states
items.meaningCN: 容易陷入低落或烦躁的
items.exampleCN: 考试前他变得闷闷不乐。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a name for the trait.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成该特质的名称。

items.meaning: the trait of changing mood quickly
items.exampleCN: 情绪多变在青春期很常见。

items.meaning: music chosen to create an atmosphere
items.meaningCN: 为营造气氛而选的音乐
items.example: The café plays mood music all afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆整个下午放着氛围音乐。

items.example: The doctor asked about mood swings.
items.exampleCN: 医生询问了情绪波动的情况。

items.structure: Latin modus (source of the grammar sense)
items.example: The grammar sense is a separate Latin borrowing.
items.exampleCN: 语法义是一次独立的拉丁借入。

definition_zh: 月亮；月球；卫星；（诗）月光；（动词）闲荡、出神；（英俚）露出臀部
definition_en: the natural body that orbits the earth, or any natural satellite of a planet
core_image: 院墙上方一轮圆月升到屋脊那么高，瓦片被照出淡蓝色的光
scene: 院墙上方，一轮圆月升到屋脊那么高，瓦片被照出淡蓝的光。Above the courtyard wall, the moon has risen level with the roof tiles.
sceneCN: 这里 moon 指「绕地球运行的天然卫星，即月球」（第 1 个义项：地球的天然卫星）；句意为院墙上方，月亮已升到与屋瓦齐高。图中可辨识物件：院墙、圆月、屋脊、瓦片、淡蓝月色；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 闲荡、出神；（英俚）露出臀部

月光照亮的
月光
小卫星
